name: dithercn
capabilities: dithercn draws every surface as ordered-dither cells tied to your shadcn theme tokens, so a globe, an aurora shader and a headline fill all share one pixel grid and palette. The components install as plain source into your project, so you edit them like your own code instead of configuring a black-box package.

The chart and interface examples render as plain SVG built from whole dither cells, snapped to device pixels, so bars, gauges and heatmap squares step through crisp Bayer densities rather than opacity. Each chart keeps a hidden data table and keyboard scrubbing, so the 1-bit look does not cost accessibility.
installs: npx shadcn@latest add https://dithercn.dev/r/bar-chart.json https://dithercn.dev/r/gauge.json https://dithercn.dev/r/heatmap.json

name: Paper Shaders
capabilities: Paper's Dithering shader runs 2-colour ordered or random dithering over seven animated sources (sphere, warp, swirl, ripple...) entirely on the GPU in one small fragment shader. Every parameter is a prop, so matrix size, pixel size and ink colour can change live without remounting the canvas.

Each shader ships with named design presets (mesh gradients, grain, warp, metaballs, god rays, voronoi), so a whole art-directed background is one component spread with a preset's params. The same shaders can be designed in the Paper editor and exported as code.

LiquidMetal, Heatmap and GemSmoke take any SVG or PNG logo and turn its silhouette into animated chrome, thermal glow or smoke; the shape is pre-processed into a distance field in the browser. Pointer position drives the shaders' angle prop, so the reflections follow the cursor.

FlutedGlass, Water, HalftoneCmyk, HalftoneDots, PaperTexture, LensDistortion and ImageDithering each take an image prop and run in one fragment shader, with no canvas code to write. Every slider maps to a real prop, and holding the button shows the untouched Vermeer underneath.

PulsingBorder draws a soft, smoky light along a rounded rectangle. Here it frames a chat composer and switches props between idle, generating and done states. Because colors, pulse, bloom and smoke are plain props, React state can drive the border directly.

GodRays and SmokeRing make a full-bleed hero background with no video files, and each scene is about ten props. The light source leans toward the pointer, and the presets switch between warm volumetric rays, an eclipse ring and teal light.

A seeded RNG picks one of seven pattern shaders (Waves, Swirl, Spiral, Voronoi, NeuroNoise, PerlinNoise, SimplexNoise), a palette and props to make a print-style record sleeve. The props are shown as code, and the poster can stay animated or freeze on a frame.

Eight shaders (Metaballs, ColorPanels, Voronoi, DotOrbit, PulsingBorder, SmokeRing, Spiral, Swirl) run at icon size as activity indicators, alongside a SimplexNoise progress bar. Speed is a prop, so hovering a tile speeds it up and clicking it marks the task complete.

The React package wraps @paper-design/shaders, which works without a framework: new ShaderMount(el, fragmentShader, uniforms) and setUniforms(). Here the pointer drives the static radial gradient's focal point as a lit sphere, flinging the pointer adds ripples, and a live readout shows every uniform as it changes.

name: three.js AsciiEffect
capabilities: AsciiEffect samples the WebGL frame each tick and rewrites it as a grid of real DOM characters, so the output is selectable text you can tint, glow and style with CSS. Swapping the character ramp changes the look completely, from classic terminal to Unicode shade blocks.

name: pixi-filters
capabilities: pixi-filters bundles dozens of stackable post-process shaders (CRT, RGB split, glitch, pixelate, ASCII, old film, bloom) that attach to any PixiJS container as a plain filters array. Order in the array is the order of the effect chain, so you can build a CRT pipeline in a few lines.

name: postprocessing
capabilities: postprocessing merges multiple effects into a single fullscreen shader pass, which keeps a stack of bloom, vignette and stylising effects cheap. Its PixelationEffect, ASCIIEffect and DotScreenEffect turn any three.js scene into pixel art, glyphs or print halftone with one constructor.

name: Ratzilla
capabilities: Ratzilla runs Rust's ratatui widget library in a web page: the same Gauge, Sparkline, BarChart, Table and braille Canvas you'd use in a real terminal, drawn by a WebGL2 glyph-atlas backend. The layout is ratatui's constraint solver, so the dashboard restacks into one column on a phone. Everything here, including the braille world map and lissajous, is Rust compiled to a single .wasm.

name: dotmax
capabilities: dotmax packs 2×4 dots into every Unicode braille cell, so a terminal (or a <pre>) gets eight times the pixels of plain text. This is the crate's real BrailleGrid and line/circle/colour primitives compiled to wasm32, with the terminal-only modules stripped, writing coloured braille text into a <pre> that re-fits on resize. Five effects: plasma, black hole, ribbons and more.

name: drawille-canvas
capabilities: drawille-canvas implements the familiar moveTo/lineTo/stroke, save/translate/scale context API, but its output is a string of braille characters instead of pixels. Five wireframes (geodesic sphere, tesseract, torus, trefoil knot, stella octangula) are stroked over a Bayer-dithered plasma set dot by dot with raw drawille. Four coloured <pre> layers stack into one image.

name: rot.js
capabilities: rot.js gives you the whole roguelike stack in the browser: a character-cell Display, dungeon generators, shadowcasting field of view, A* paths and coloured light. Here a Digger dungeon is generated to the viewport, walls are drawn as braille masonry, and a flickering torch plus ROT.Lighting glow decide what you see. Leave it idle and an A* auto-explorer loots, fights and descends.

name: textmode.js
capabilities: textmode.js has a p5-style sketch API (push, rotate, rect, torus, lights), but it rasterises everything into a grid of characters on the GPU. The torus uses the library's own pointLight and torus(), so the lighting is computed per cell. Four sketches (tunnel, lit solids, flow field, copper bars) run on its bundled CP437 pixel font.

name: play.core
capabilities: play.core is the engine behind the ASCII Playground: a program exports a main(coord, context, cursor) function that returns one character per cell, and the runner sizes the grid from font metrics and renders it as DOM text. Four programs run here: SDF braille metaballs, copper bars, braille rain and an adapted Doom flame. It is unpublished on npm and vendored from GitHub.

name: ascii-magic-art
capabilities: Each piece is a tiny ES module whose draw(t) returns a frame of text plus a colour layer. The player repaints it on a canvas, and can redraw any piece live in another 'look' (halftone dots, binary, dither, blocks…) without restarting. Thirty curated pieces from seven categories, scaled to fit any screen.

ascii-magic-art ships whole categories of empty-state and loader pieces. A mail-client mock uses them as illustrations, cropped to the drawing so real HTML supplies the heading and buttons. Each tab cycles empty → loading (skeleton, progress and upload loaders) → results, and the Online toggle switches to an offline-plug animation.

name: asciichart + figlet
capabilities: asciichart turns number series into box-drawing line charts (╭╮╰╯) with ANSI colours; figlet.js renders FIGlet banner fonts. Three streaming chart panels are sized to the available columns, and the FIGlet clock cycles through six bundled fonts, shrinking to fit narrow screens. Tapping a chart injects an incident that appears in the syslog tail.

name: cli-spinners
capabilities: cli-spinners is just data: each spinner is a list of frames and an interval, which is why it works in any terminal library or web page. All 71 non-emoji spinners run at their native interval from one rAF loop, colour-coded by family (braille dots, lines, blocks, arrows). The selected one drives a fake install line with a braille progress bar.

name: Matrix digital rain (Rezmason)
capabilities: Each glyph is an MSDF texture sampled in a fragment shader, so the film fonts stay sharp at any size, and the rain is simulated on the GPU in ping-pong framebuffers before a bloom pyramid and palette pass. One config object switches between the 1999 grid, the Resurrections glyph set, volumetric 3D rain, polar Coptic ripples and a slanted gothic storm with thunder.

name: AnsiLove.js
capabilities: AnsiLove.js parses .ANS, .BIN, .XB, .ADF, .IDF and .PCB files in the browser and paints them with the original bitmap fonts: IBM VGA, VGA50, Amiga Topaz, P0T-NOoDLE, MicroKnight. It handles iCE colors, SAUCE metadata and baud-rate playback, so ANSI art scrolls in at modem speed. All three pieces in this demo are original ANSIs generated in code.

name: glyphcss
capabilities: glyphcss projects real 3D geometry (OBJ, glTF, STL, .vox or its own primitives) and rasterizes it into a single monospace <pre>, with no WebGL, no canvas and no per-polygon DOM nodes. The same scene switches between Lambert-shaded ramps, 2×2 quadrant blocks, hidden-line braille wireframe and contour-tracing ink mode, so the output is selectable text you can style with CSS.

name: Asciify
capabilities: asciify-engine's /kit turns interface states into character animation with one call each: a loading button whose label cycles through glyphs, a border beam that becomes a progress ring, tabs with a streaking glyph rule, odometer figures and block-character charts. Every field shares one WebGL2 context, takes its ink from CSS custom properties, pauses off screen and leaves plain HTML in place when no GPU is available.

name: svgbob (WASM)
capabilities: svgbob reads plain-text diagrams the way a person does: '.-' becomes a rounded corner, '*' a node, 'o' a commit circle, and '-->' an arrow with a real marker. The output is plain SVG with classed lines, paths and polygons, so a few CSS rules restyle the whole diagram, and the source stays readable in a README or code comment.

name: ASCII FX
capabilities: Most ASCII filters pick a glyph by how much ink it has; ASCII FX matches each cell's 8×8 sample block against every glyph's real rasterised mask, so diagonals become / and \ and type stays legible. The split view runs the library's own brightness-ramp matcher against its structural matcher on the same font and grid, in WebGPU compute or bit-identical CPU workers.

name: glyphcast
capabilities: glyphcast samples each video frame into a cell grid and draws it with a WebGL2 shader as braille dots, ASCII ramps, shade blocks or halftone, with per-cell colour, contour glyphs and a CRT look, live and switchable. It also ships a compact .gcast glyph-stream format that plays the same in a browser or a terminal.

name: The Monospace Web
capabilities: Every element sits on a lattice exactly 1ch wide and one line tall: headings, tables, inputs, trees, figures and buttons. Plain semantic HTML gets a terminal-printout look, with no utility classes. A small script pads images down to the next row, and a debug toggle shows the underlying grid.

name: crt-terminal
capabilities: A React terminal that prints output through an event queue: lines stream in at a set speed, a loader locks input while it spins, and arrow-up walks command history. Scanlines, pixel mask, glow pulse and screen shiver come built in, and every element exposes a stable class, so the whole tube re-skins with CSS variables (amber, green and ice phosphor here). Output words can be buttons or links, so the help screen is clickable.

name: asciinema-player
capabilities: Replays asciicast files as selectable, copyable text rather than video: truecolor and 256-color SGR, alternate-screen TUIs and cursor-addressed redraws all render on a crisp monospace grid. Themes are plain CSS variables, chapter markers come from the cast itself, and the JS API (seek, marker events, play/pause) lets you build your own transport. The 40-second session here is synthesized by a Python script, not recorded.

name: @thi.ng/text-canvas
capabilities: A character grid you draw on like a canvas: stroke rects in single, double, dashed or rounded box styles, clip regions, plot line charts, block-element bar charts and full tables, all with per-cell color formats. formatCanvas() serializes the result as ANSI, plain text or HTML spans, so the same dashboard can run in a terminal or a <pre>.

name: Pretext
capabilities: Pretext measures and line-breaks text without touching the DOM, so you can re-layout a paragraph against arbitrary shapes every frame. Here two justified columns of Walden are re-broken around a draggable moon (and its own label) on each animation frame, using a per-row width and a shared cursor across columns, in well under 2 ms.

Because Pretext returns line breaks and widths without rendering, every grapheme can become a physics particle that knows exactly where it belongs. Quotes are laid out with layoutWithLines, framed by the tightest shrink-wrap width from measureLineStats, then morph letter by letter into the next quote.

name: GSAP SplitText
capabilities: SplitText wraps lines, words and characters in elements (with optional line masks and auto re-split on resize), and ScrambleText decodes strings through random glyphs. Four click-through choreographies (rise, flip, scatter, decode) share one split; hovering a word makes it jump and re-decode.

name: NumberFlow
capabilities: NumberFlow animates between Intl.NumberFormat outputs digit by digit, rolling each column and morphing separators and widths when the format changes. A live Voyager 1 distance board ticks every second; switching km / mi / AU morphs the whole format, and a time-warp slider spins decades of digits.

name: Rough Notation
capabilities: Rough Notation draws sketchy SVG underlines, boxes, circles, highlights, strike-throughs and brackets over live DOM text using rough.js, and animates the stroke as if drawn by hand. An annotationGroup plays an editor's pass over Strunk's Rule 17; then you pick a mark and annotate any word yourself.

name: Shiki
capabilities: Shiki highlights code with the same TextMate grammars and themes as VS Code, so output matches the editor exactly, and it runs fully in the browser with a pure-JS regex engine (no WASM). The same snippet cross-fades through eight themes; swatches are built from each theme's own token colours and hovering a token shows its TextMate scope.

name: Splitting.js
capabilities: Splitting.js makes one pass over the DOM, wrapping each word and character and giving it --char-index and --char-total custom properties; everything after that is plain CSS. A registered @property sweeps a highlight across the word, and each letter computes its own variable-font weight, softness, colour and lift from its distance to it.

name: Vara
capabilities: Vara draws text stroke by stroke from single-line font files, so letters appear in pen order instead of fading in. A Keats couplet is written out and re-written in four script hands; type your own line and Vara writes it on the ruled pad.

name: blotter.ts
capabilities: blotter.ts is a typed ESM rewrite of Bradley Griffith's Blotter: text goes into a shared atlas, a Shadertoy-style material shader runs over it, and each word gets its own output canvas. One word cycles through the bundled Liquid, Rolling, Channel-split, Sliding-door and Flies materials. Your pointer drives their live uniforms, and the current values are printed under the word.

name: Hanzi Writer
capabilities: Hanzi Writer renders each character as SVG stroke paths from the Make Me a Hanzi dataset, so it can animate the correct stroke order, colour the radical separately and grade a user's freehand strokes one by one. Here it runs on a rice-grid pad in ink and vermilion, cycling through 永 書 龍 中 字 道 until you switch to the trace quiz.

name: Shiki Magic Move
capabilities: Magic Move diffs two highlighted snippets and gives every matching token a stable key, so unchanged code glides to its new position while removed tokens fade out and new ones fade in. Here one function morphs from callback hell to promises, async/await, types and memoization, using Shiki's fine-grained core with the JavaScript regex engine and only TypeScript plus the Vesper theme.

name: three-slug
capabilities: three-slug evaluates each glyph's quadratic Béziers in the fragment shader, so text has exact coverage at any zoom, and it splices into MeshStandardMaterial for real lighting and shadows. The camera dives from a lit word into one curve, shown with its control polygon, down to about ×2,000 where the edge is still a one-pixel ramp; the bitmap dot-grid wall goes soft at that zoom.

name: mejiro
capabilities: mejiro measures every glyph and breaks Japanese vertical text the way a print typesetter would: kinsoku shori, hanging punctuation, ruby, tate-chu-yoko and real pagination, from a DOM-free core. Here it sets the opening chapters of Miyazawa Kenji's Night on the Galactic Railroad (Aozora Bunko, public domain) into a right-to-left book that re-paginates live on resize, text size or hanging-punctuation changes.

name: Justif
capabilities: Browsers justify one line at a time, which leaves stretched word spaces and rivers of white. Justif re-breaks real HTML paragraphs with Knuth–Plass, TeX hyphenation patterns, protrusion and tiny tracking adjustments, and stays a progressive enhancement. This duel sets the same Moby-Dick paragraph both ways at a shared width and colours every word space by how far it stretched.

name: three-text
capabilities: three-text shapes real font files with HarfBuzz, breaks paragraphs with Knuth–Plass plus Liang hyphenation, then tessellates every glyph into extrudable, lightable three.js geometry. Here a variable-font paragraph re-justifies live as the measure changes, with margin rules and amber ticks marking each hyphenated break.

name: Heti 赫蹏
capabilities: Heti is a stylesheet plus a small add-on script that follow Chinese typesetting rules (clreq). Its classes set classical text in right-to-left vertical columns with emphasis dots, and the add-on inserts quarter-em gaps between Han characters and Latin letters or digits and squeezes adjacent full-width punctuation. Flip Heti off to see the same markup with browser defaults; the marks show each gap it inserted.

name: type-hangul
capabilities: Most typewriter effects add whole characters, but Hangul syllables are built from jamo: ㅎ → 하 → 한, and a final consonant can jump to the next syllable (한 + ㅏ → 하나). type-hangul replays that two-set keyboard composition, and its per-keystroke events drive the composing readout and the lit 두벌식 keys here. The text is Yun Dong-ju's public-domain poem “Seosi” with an English gloss, and you can type your own Korean.

name: feral fur
capabilities: feral fur paints thousands of individual strands onto one canvas, rooted inside a silhouette (a built-in shape, an SVG path, or a line of text, counters included) with a fringe that pokes past the edge. Strands bend under the pointer and spring back, and the loop sleeps when nothing moves. Here a ghost paw keeps stroking the word until you take over; coat colour, fluff and mess are all props.

name: Code Hike
capabilities: Code Hike turns comment annotations like !focus, !mark, !callout and !diff into React components you write yourself, so code blocks can carry callouts, diffs and focus states. Its selection utilities connect scrolling prose to the code, which makes scrollycoding tutorials a few components instead of a custom framework.

name: growtype
capabilities: growtype sets each character on its own wobbly stalk rooted in a path, with flared feet, side branches, floating spores, a travelling gust of wind and four stages of wilting, all as one self-contained SVG with embedded CSS keyframes. Draw any line and the phrase sprouts along it; the wilt toggle re-renders with an advancing timeOffset so every sprout slumps and springs back in turn.

name: Burn-In.js
capabilities: Burn-In.js rasterises a text mask from the real DOM glyphs, ignites fire and smoke particles along the letterforms on an overlay canvas, then hands back ordinary selectable text. Six presets (ritual, wildfire, smolder, flash, soft, psycho) and a font-size scale basis keep the flames proportional to each line, so a whole letter can burn in line by line.

name: Postext
capabilities: Postext typesets enriched markdown the way print editors work: Knuth–Plass optimal line breaking, hyphenation, widow and orphan control, a shared baseline grid, balanced columns, drop caps and footnotes at the foot of the column. buildDocument returns a tree of every page, line and box, which you can paint to canvas or HTML, and it can flag loose lines for you.

name: opentype.js
capabilities: opentype.js reads a font file into real objects: glyph outlines as path commands, cmap, metrics and kerning. That makes a type-design inspector possible in plain JS. Here bundled WOFF fonts are parsed in the browser, and each glyph's quadratic outline is traced with its on-curve points, off-curve points and metric lines.

name: Wavefont + Linefont
capabilities: Each character U+0100–U+017F is one data value: Wavefont draws it as a bar, Linefont as a connected line segment. So waveforms, spectra and sparklines are ordinary selectable text, styled by variable axes for width, roundness and alignment. Every trace here is a string rewritten 30 times a second; the raw toggle shows the actual characters.

name: Glitched Writer
capabilities: Glitched Writer animates a string into another through ghost characters, per-letter steps and write modes (matching, normal, erase, clear), with presets like nier, encrypted, neo, zalgo, bitbybit and cosmic. Letterize mode wraps every character in spans so ghosts and glitched letters can be styled separately. Six writers here decode the same sentence in a rolling wave, and you can type your own.

name: CircleType
capabilities: CircleType splits real DOM text into letters and rotates each one onto a circle. Text stays selectable and can use any font, with radius and direction (.radius(), .dir()) adjustable live. The seal sets three full rings in Syne, Instrument Serif and JetBrains Mono, one counter-clockwise; the headline's arc bends as you drag.

name: Tegaki
capabilities: Tegaki ships font bundles with skeleton strokes and pen pressure extracted from regular OFL fonts, so Parisienne, Caveat, Japanese Klee One or Korean Nanum Pen get written stroke by stroke in a believable order instead of wiped in with a mask. Plugins reshape the ink (taper, glow, boil, gradients) and the engine exposes the live pen position per frame.

name: glyphShaper
capabilities: glyphShaper parses the font binary client-side, lets you move a glyph's Bézier points, then patches just that glyph back into the TrueType file and re-injects it as an @font-face override. Every instance of the letter on the page re-renders, and kerning, hinting and other tables are copied byte-for-byte.

name: beer-text
capabilities: beer-text runs a small physics simulation, not a looping wave: the stream lands, the surface sloshes, a foam head builds and decays, and bubbles rise inside the letter shapes, drawn in SVG and canvas over the heading. The heading stays real, selectable text in its own web font, and five presets (lager to stout) recolor the whole pour.

name: tightset
capabilities: tightset picks the line breaks that let every line run the full width of a box, then gives bigger lines heavier weights from a variable font, so any rectangle gets poster-style hierarchy. Here the frame breathes and can be dragged; each frame calls fit() again and the quote re-breaks live, drawn with tightset/canvas.

name: Ztext (react-ztext)
capabilities: A React port of Bennett Feely's Ztext: it clones any text into N layers spread along translateZ inside a preserve-3d wrapper, then tilts the stack toward the pointer. Because every layer is ordinary DOM text in your own font, CSS can colour each slice, so a gradient through the layers reads as a lit extrusion and the front face stays selectable.

name: ghostdust
capabilities: ghostdust samples text, SVG or image pixels into roughly 15k WebGL points, each pulled home by a spring, so a sweep of the cursor or a finger parts the letters like dust before they settle back. Physics params are live on the engine and setText/setSvg swap content on a running instance: here a warm Fraunces wordmark re-forms into an SVG ghost mark while an idle wisp keeps it moving.

name: glyphdust
capabilities: glyphdust is one react-three-fiber component driven by a single 0 to 1 progress value: keyframes dissolve a real heading into GPU particles, scatter them, form any SVG path, then cross-fade into crisp, selectable DOM text placed exactly over the glyph it formed. Here you scrub that timeline by hand, as NOISE in Unbounded becomes a particle waveform and resolves as 'signal' in Instrument Serif under the selective-bloom glow preset.

name: glyphed.js
capabilities: Every letter is a real monoline glyph path, not a font, with random variants and jitter per render, and the icons, hatched charts and circles/strikes go through the same sketch engine, so a heading, a donut chart and an underline all share one pen. Strokes draw in with plain stroke-dashoffset transitions, and roughness plus seed set how shaky the hand is.

name: confettiText
capabilities: confettiText ports canvas-confetti's physics (spread, velocity, decay, gravity, 3D paper flip) to DOM spans, so each piece is a glyph from your own string in your own web font. A per-particle wght range turns a variable font like Fraunces into confetti of mixed weights, and paper strips or circles can be mixed in.

name: Paged.js
capabilities: Paged.js reads @page rules the browser ignores on screen (page size, mirrored left/right margins, margin boxes, named pages, string-set running heads, page counters, float: footnote) and flows the HTML into real page boxes. This demo hands it one CSS file and a public-domain chapter of Alice. Running heads, folios, a drop cap and a footnote come out as fixed pages, which the demo then sets in a spread you can turn.

name: threadText
capabilities: threadText runs each glyph through a distance field and a flow field, then lays thousands of pre-lit thread sprites across every stroke and sews them in row by row. The result is raised floss with a cursor sheen. It is not a raster filter. Satin, chain, cross and running textures plus solid, two-tone or gradient floss all switch live.

name: Markdeep
capabilities: Markdeep turns plain text into a typeset document in the browser, and its stand-out trick is diagrams: boxes, rounded corners, arrows, diagonals and junction dots drawn in ASCII become clean SVG on the same 8×16 character grid. Here the source and the rendered SVG sit in exact register under a wipe, so you can see each character's vector counterpart. MathJax loading is turned off, so there are no external requests.

name: Tufte CSS
capabilities: Tufte CSS lays out a page like Tufte's own books: a narrow text column in ET Book on cream paper, numbered sidenotes and margin figures in a wide right margin, small-caps new thoughts and epigraphs. On phones the notes fold into tap toggles built from plain checkboxes, with no JavaScript. Here it frames an essay with a word-sized sparkline, a margin chart and twelve linked small multiples.

name: Zfont
capabilities: Zfont parses a .ttf with Typr.js and turns every glyph into Zdog path commands, so type becomes ordinary flat-shaded Zdog shapes that rotate in 3D. Stacking Text copies along z gives chunky extruded lettering, and one Text per glyph sets type on a ring. Both sit next to hand-built Zdog characters.

name: spoilerjs
capabilities: A dependency-free <spoiler-span> that measures each line box of its text and covers it with a canvas of drifting 1-2px particles in the text's own colour. Tapping it stops the spawning and the noise thins away to show the text. It works on inline text, wrapped lines and whole elements, so a blurred photo can be a spoiler too.

name: FlowToken
capabilities: FlowToken diffs each new chunk of a streaming markdown string and animates only the fresh slice, so earlier words stay still while new tokens blur, drop, wave or glow in. It ships 13 CSS entrances and passes any custom keyframe name straight through, including inside highlighted code blocks.

name: Smart Ticker
capabilities: Smart Ticker runs a Levenshtein diff between the old and new string, so only the characters that changed roll through their character list while inserted and deleted columns slide their width in or out. It handles any string, including CJK and Hangul with full-width spacing, and this demo prints the library's own edit script under every step.

name: LaTeX.css
capabilities: Drop in one stylesheet and plain HTML picks up Latin Modern type, a centred title and author block, an abstract, booktabs-style table rules and numbered captions; a few opt-in classes add theorem and proof blocks. Here the paper's real source sits beside the typeset page and a linked inspector tours h1 → equation → theorem → proof → table → footnotes. The math is plain HTML entities, no KaTeX or MathJax, and .latex-dark flips the theme.

name: Torph
capabilities: Torph diffs the old and new string and slides shared letters to their new positions, so 'listen' becomes 'silent' with every letter travelling and nothing fading out. Numbers morph by place value: the digits that changed roll and the rest stay put. For a text field, pass the caret index and it matches by caret position instead.

name: harfbuzzjs
capabilities: harfbuzzjs exposes what the browser does internally: which glyph IDs a string becomes, their advances and offsets, and which code points each glyph came from. Here Arabic letters change their joining form as each new letter is typed, Devanagari moves its i-matra in front of the consonant and lifts the reph above it, and EB Garamond builds ligatures and fractions. Glyph outlines are drawn straight from glyphToPath, and you can toggle each OpenType feature to see the result change.

name: Windups
capabilities: Windups types out any React children one character at a time and handles timing for you: it pauses on punctuation by default, and <Pace> and <Pause> set a speed or a beat inside a line. <CharWrapper> wraps each character in its own element, which is how the wobbly and trembling words animate. <OnChar> drives the frog's mouth and the optional synth blips. <Linebreaker> works out line breaks before typing starts, so words never jump to the next line halfway through.

name: magnetType
capabilities: magnetType wraps each word in a span and sets its font-variation-settings from the pointer's distance, so a paragraph swells heavier and wider around the cursor and relaxes behind it. Built-in layout stabilisation cancels each word's width change with letter-spacing, so lines never reflow. Here a Fraunces headline (wght/opsz/SOFT) and a Roboto Flex column (wght/wdth/GRAD) each run their own field, with a phantom cursor drifting on a Lissajous path when idle.

name: FloodText
capabilities: FloodText wraps every grapheme and drives weight, width, oblique angle or opacity along a travelling sine, so each letter sits at its own point on the wave. Line breaks stay locked and kerning is preserved while glyph widths change, so the poem never reflows. This demo layers axes on a Roboto Flex poem, with controls for direction and swell and a WCAG pause button.

name: BrowserTextEffects
capabilities: A TypeScript port of TerminalTextEffects: laser etch, burn, matrix rain, synthgrid, fireworks and 32 more, each driving a real grid of monospace character cells with per-cell color gradients, easing and particle paths. Hand it any multi-line string (here, block-letter ASCII art generated in code) and a container, and it lays the characters out on a fixed cell grid and animates them with no canvas.

name: use-springface
capabilities: Each glyph gets its own spring on any font-variation axis, so letters near the pointer swell in width, weight and cap height and then overshoot back. A stacked multi-color text-shadow points away from the cursor. It writes inline styles from one requestAnimationFrame loop and never re-renders React, which keeps a giant Roboto Flex wordmark smooth.

name: Cobe
capabilities: Cobe draws a Fibonacci-sampled dot-matrix Earth in a single fragment shader, with no three.js and zero deps. Version 2 adds arcs and exposes every marker as a CSS anchor, so the labels here are plain DOM elements placed with CSS anchor positioning and faded by a --cobe-visible-* variable.

name: Vanta.js
capabilities: Vanta wraps three.js scenes and shaders (halo, fog, net, waves, flocking birds) into drop-in background effects that track the mouse. You pass an element, a THREE instance and a palette; destroy() tears it down, which is what this switcher does.

name: WebGL Fluid
capabilities: This is a real Navier-Stokes solver running on the GPU: advection, pressure and curl passes, then bloom and sunrays post-processing. The webgl-fluid package turns the well-known demo into one function call with options for auto-splats, trigger mode and dissipation.

name: ShaderGradient
capabilities: ShaderGradient displaces a plane, water plane or sphere with noise and shades it with three colors plus film grain, which gives the soft, moving gradients you see on landing pages. Every look is a small set of props, so presets can be swapped and tweened.

name: OGL
capabilities: OGL is a small, dependency-free WebGL abstraction with renderer, program, mesh and an extras folder. Its Flowmap helper ping-pongs render targets to record cursor velocity, and here that velocity drives a per-channel RGB-split warp of a procedurally drawn poster.

name: Zdog
capabilities: Zdog renders 3D models as flat 2D strokes, so everything gets round caps and solid fills, like vector illustration that can rotate. Shapes are composed from anchors, hemispheres, cones and paths, and dragRotate gives you an interactive scene in a few lines.

name: threejs-toys
capabilities: Kevin Levron's threejs-toys packages shader-heavy effects as single functions: an SDF-bezier neon tube that follows the cursor, a GPGPU particle cursor, and an instanced swarm. Each takes an element and a config object and creates its own renderer.

name: tsParticles
capabilities: tsParticles is a plugin-based rewrite of particles.js. Shapes, links, interactions and updaters are separate packages, and the whole scene is one options object. With link triangles enabled, neighbouring particles fill in as translucent faces, which gives a moving low-poly mesh.

name: TypeGPU
capabilities: TypeGPU describes GPU memory with schemas (d.struct, d.arrayOf, d.atomic) so buffer writes, bind-group layouts and the generated WGSL bindings all come from one typed definition. Here thousands of boids run in a three-pass spatial-grid compute pipeline and draw as flapping chevrons into a fading float accumulation buffer.

name: GSS (GPU Style Sheets)
capabilities: You write @scene, selectors, the cascade, @keyframes, var() and :hover, and the compiler resolves them into GLSL/WGSL signed-distance shaders, with no meshes or Three.js. This editor recompiles the stylesheet in the page as you type, keeps the last good scene on a syntax error, and points to the line.

name: React Fluid Distortion
capabilities: Drop <Fluid /> into an @react-three/postprocessing EffectComposer and everything in the scene, including type, smears behind the cursor. It runs a Navier–Stokes simulation (after Pavel Dobryakov's WebGL fluid) and uses the velocity field to warp UVs. Modes set colour: rainbow by flow direction, a single ink, or pure glass refraction.

name: fireworks-js
capabilities: A dependency-free canvas-2D fireworks engine where hue range, gravity, friction, decay, flicker and trail fade are all plain options you can update while it runs. Press-and-hold aiming is built in. Here it runs over a procedural skyline, and the canvas is mirrored into rippling harbor reflections and a bloom layer.

name: color4bg
capabilities: color4bg ships 14 ready-made background generators (wavy satin, contour swirls, low-poly mosaics, floating cubes) built on a tiny OGL core. Each one takes up to six colours and a seed, so the same pattern reproduces exactly and a palette swap is one colors() call, no image files involved.

name: Shaders
capabilities: Every effect is a component: generators like MeshGradient, Aurora and Satin stack like Figma layers with real blend modes, and filters (CursorRipples, Dither, FilmGrain) apply to everything above them. Props accept pointer drivers such as { type: 'mouse-position' }, so cursor-reactive motion takes no animation code. This hero switches between four compositions of one <Shader>.

The vanilla shaders/js API takes a JSON component tree, so an image filter is just ImageTexture plus an effect: a refracting Glass solid (sphere, torus, gem, blob) with chromatic aberration and frost, FlutedGlass, CMYK Halftone or a CRTScreen. Sliders call shader.update() live, and mode switches cross-fade between trees that share one WebGPU device.

name: Shader Lab (basement.studio)
capabilities: Plays compositions from basement.studio's Shader Lab editor. Each one is a flat JSON stack: gradient and text sources under post passes such as Bayer dithering, slot-mask CRT, SDF-glyph ASCII and CMYK halftone, compiled to three.js TSL. It renders through WebGPURenderer, which falls back to WebGL2. Every layer param is plain data, so you can drive it from pointer input each frame.

name: use-shader-fx
capabilities: Each hook (useFluid, useNoise, useBuffer, useBlank) renders into its own FBO and returns a texture, so effects chain like nodes: here a Navier-Stokes fluid's flow map is fed into useNoise's built-in mixSrc UV-displacement to stir a domain-warped marble field. v2's shared 'basicFx' layer gives every hook mix, levels, HSV and duotone options without writing GLSL.

name: three.quarks
capabilities: Game-engine particle authoring in code: emitter shapes, over-life behaviors (color, size, orbit, gravity, turbulence), trail ribbons, stretched billboards and sub-emitters. A BatchedRenderer merges dozens of systems into a handful of draw calls; here 63 systems render in about 7 batches.

name: three-nebula
capabilities: Every system here is a plain JSON object (emitters, initializers, behaviours), in the same shape the Nebula visual editor exports, and is turned into a live system with System.fromJSONAsync. Behaviours like Vortex, CurlNoise, Attraction and Repulsion combine into flow fields, so a two-armed galaxy is just two emitters feeding one Vortex. GPURenderer draws each system as a single batched THREE.Points.

name: three-raymarcher
capabilities: A drop-in three.js Mesh that raymarches signed-distance primitives with smooth union, subtraction and intersection, lit by a PMREM env map. Its depth output composites with ordinary meshes, so the chrome ring here really passes through the goo, and the built-in raycasting lets you grab individual blobs.

name: three-good-godrays
capabilities: A postprocessing pass that raymarches each pixel's view ray through the light's shadow map, so shafts are cut by the actual geometry rather than smeared radially in screen space. Here a point light sits inside an 80-panel perforated icosphere: every hole throws its own beam, and the dark wedges between them rotate with the lattice. Density, attenuation, color and step count are live parameters.

name: drei materials
capabilities: MeshTransmissionMaterial renders real refraction: it samples the scene behind the mesh with chromatic aberration, anisotropic blur and backside thickness, so bold type warps through the glass. MeshDistortMaterial and MeshWobbleMaterial are noise-displaced physical materials in one prop each. The studio reflections come from <Lightformer> cards, so no HDR file is downloaded.

name: Spark
capabilities: Spark draws photo-captured 3D gaussian splats next to ordinary three.js meshes and treats every splat as editable on the GPU. Here a 240k-splat CC0 cactus scan is relit with SplatEdit SDF light spheres and scattered by a custom dyno shader-graph block. It reads .spz, .ply, .splat, .ksplat and .sog files.

name: <model-viewer>
capabilities: One HTML tag gives you an orbitable, auto-rotating PBR product view with neutral studio lighting, soft shadows and DOM hotspots pinned to model coordinates. It supports glTF extensions like KHR_materials_sheen (the velvet glow) and KHR_materials_variants, so fabric swaps are one property change, not a second download.

name: react-three-rapier
capabilities: Wrap meshes in <RigidBody> and react-three-rapier generates colliders (ball, cuboid, convex hull) from the geometry, then steps the WebAssembly Rapier simulation in sync with R3F's render loop. A kinematic body follows your pointer to shove clear-coated candy shapes around a tray, and gravity is just a prop.

name: three.js WebGPU + TSL
capabilities: TSL builds shaders from composable JavaScript nodes (noise, palettes, fresnel, uniforms) and compiles them to WGSL for WebGPU or GLSL for the WebGL2 fallback. Displacement, contour bands and rim glow here are all node graphs on a MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial, with no shader strings. The badge shows which backend your browser got.

name: Theatre.js
capabilities: Theatre.js plays back keyframed, bezier-eased sequences of any props: camera position, look-at target, FOV and light color here. The project state is the same JSON its visual Studio exports, so @theatre/core alone (Apache-2.0, no editor UI) drives the animation. The custom timeline scrubs sheet.sequence.position directly.

name: CustomShaderMaterial
capabilities: three-custom-shader-material injects your vertex/fragment code into any built-in material and keeps its lighting, shadows and PBR features. The same displacement-plus-recomputed-normals shader runs here on Physical (iridescent clearcoat), Toon, Matcap and Normal base materials. You write csm_Position and csm_Normal instead of rewriting a lighting model.

name: Neat
capabilities: Neat displaces a WebGL mesh with noise and shades it with highlights, shadows, flow-field distortion and film grain, so gradients read as lit, moving surfaces instead of flat CSS blends. Every property is a live setter, so this demo crossfades four configs by tweening numbers, and flips one preset into wireframe to show the mesh underneath. Free builds render a small NEAT watermark; a paid key removes it.

name: Takram three-geospatial
capabilities: Implements Bruneton's precomputed atmospheric scattering in real ECEF coordinates: you give it a lat/long and a Date, and it computes the true sun position, sky radiance, sunlight transmittance and haze over distance. Here the procedural ridges fade into warm haze as you scrub through a real Alpine sunset. On hardware GPUs the companion @takram/three-clouds package adds ray-marched cloud layers lit by the same atmosphere.

name: TSL Textures
capabilities: Pavel Boytchev's library turns each texture (planet, marble, tiger fur, fordite, Dyson sphere...) into a single TSL function that returns a color node, so it compiles to WGSL or GLSL and runs on WebGPU or the WebGL2 fallback with no image files. Every parameter, including the seed, can be a uniform: here twelve swatches drift by animating their seed, and a tap reseeds one.

name: PlayCanvas Web Components
capabilities: A whole PlayCanvas scene (camera, scripts, post-processing, Gaussian splats) is written as nested tags like <pc-entity> and <pc-gsplat>, and attributes stay live: this galaxy spins because JS rewrites the disc's rotation attribute, which the corner snippet prints. The 62k-splat galaxy is a .ply generated by a small Node script, with HDR colours feeding the cameraFrame bloom.

name: Threlte
capabilities: Threlte lets you build a three.js scene graph in Svelte markup, as in <T.Mesh> and <T.MeshPhysicalMaterial>, and Svelte's reactivity drives the props. The extras package ships helpers like <Float>, <Outlines>, <Stars>, <Sparkles>, <OrbitControls> and a pointer-interactivity plugin. Here, clicking a crystal starts a Svelte Spring that pulses it and changes its color.

name: TresJS
capabilities: TresJS maps every three.js class to a Vue tag (<TresMesh>, <TresPointLight>), so Vue reactivity drives material props directly — here a click updates a ref and the cientos MeshWobbleMaterial's factor and colour follow. The cientos kit adds drop-in Levioso float, Sparkles, Stars and ContactShadows components, so a scene this size stays a short template.

name: svader
capabilities: Svader turns a fragment shader into a Svelte component: you pass a parameters array and each prop value goes straight into a uniform, with built-ins for resolution, offset and time. Four tiles here (plasma, voronoi, caustics, domain warp) each bind a slider and the pointer to uniforms, so dragging a slider updates the shader on the next frame.

name: EZ-Tree
capabilities: EZ-Tree grows a full tree mesh (tapered, twisted branches plus alpha-cut leaf cards) from one seeded options object, and a single seed reproduces the same tree every time. It ships Oak, Ash, Aspen, Pine and Bush presets, bark and leaf textures, and a leaf wind-sway shader driven by tree.update(t). This demo recolours its leaves for autumn and regrows a new seed on every tap.

name: liquid-glass-react
capabilities: Instead of a frosted backdrop-filter blur, it bends the content behind each panel with an SVG displacement map, adds chromatic aberration at the rim and stretches the glass elastically toward the pointer. The four refraction modes (standard, polar, prominent, shader) change how the edge lenses light. Full displacement renders in Chromium; Safari and Firefox fall back to a partial effect.

name: Shader Park
capabilities: You describe a 3D form with JS calls like sphere(), boxFrame(), noise() and mixGeo(), and Shader Park compiles them to a raymarched GLSL signed-distance field rendered on a three.js mesh. Shapes blend smoothly with no polygons, and uniforms like time, mouse and a click input drive them live.

name: PowerGlitch
capabilities: PowerGlitch clones an element into layers and animates clip-path slices, shake and hue-rotate with CSS keyframes, so images, text and buttons glitch without canvas or WebGL. Effects play always, on hover, on click or manually, and the whole configuration is one options object.

name: Mesh Gradient
capabilities: Four hex colours go in and a noise-displaced WebGL plane comes out, folding like fabric. Seed, frequency and speed are plain options, colour and seed changes tween smoothly, and a wireframe flag exposes the underlying mesh. It is framework-free and pauses itself when scrolled out of view.

name: GL Transitions
capabilities: Every transition is one small GLSL function, transition(uv), that mixes two textures by a progress value, so the same file runs in a browser, a video editor or ffmpeg. The npm package ships the whole community collection with author and license metadata, and gl-transition renders any entry onto a WebGL canvas.

name: curtains.js
capabilities: curtains.js keeps your layout in HTML and CSS: each element with an becomes a WebGL plane sized and positioned to match it, with the image bound as a texture uniform. You add vertex and fragment shaders for ripples, RGB splits and depth while the page stays accessible and responsive.

name: css-doodle
capabilities: A <css-doodle> element turns its contents into a grid of cells, and a small grammar (@grid, @i, @x, @r, @p, @shape) lets one CSS rule vary per cell. The result is Truchet tiles, vortices and shape fields made entirely of DOM and CSS, and update() re-rolls every random value.

name: blobs
capabilities: blobs generates organic closed shapes from a seed, point count and randomness value, then interpolates between any two of them, even with different point counts, without kinks. Output is an SVG path or a Path2D for canvas, and its keyframe API with easing callbacks makes looping morphs a few lines.

name: liquidGL
capabilities: liquidGL captures the page with its own built-in renderer (no html2canvas) and refracts it through shader-driven glass panes, with bevels, chromatic aberration, magnification, tint and a viscous 'fluid' surface. Unlike CSS backdrop-filter or SVG displacement, it truly bends the pixels under it, including GSAP animations registered as dynamic, and falls back from WebGPU to WebGL2, WebGL1, then CSS.

name: VFX-JS
capabilities: VFX-JS copies a live HTML element into a WebGL texture and redraws it each frame through a preset or custom GLSL shader, so headlines and images stay real, editable DOM. Uniforms can be functions, so pointer distance, scroll or app state feed the shader directly. Retype the headline here and the glitch follows your text.

name: three-msdf-text-utils
capabilities: Lays out bitmap-font MSDF text as three.js geometry with per-glyph attributes (letterIndex, lineIndex, center, glyphUv, layoutUv), so one ShaderMaterial can stagger, flip and dissolve each letter. The signed distance stays crisp at any zoom and doubles as data: here it drives contour lines, glows and an ember dissolve.

name: glfx.js
capabilities: glfx.js runs classic photo filters (swirl, bulge/pinch, hex pixelate, CMYK halftone, ink, tilt-shift) as WebGL shaders and chains them into one draw call. Filters are positioned in pixel space, so you can attach a distortion lens to the pointer and change parameters on every frame. It dates from 2011 and still works under a modern bundler.

name: hover-effect
capabilities: Robin Delaporte's Codrops classic: a grayscale displacement texture drives how one image melts into the next, so swapping the map changes the whole feel of the transition. Here each card gets its own generated map (wind-ripple stripes, swirly noise, cell mosaic) with its own angle and intensity.

name: Kampos
capabilities: Kampos compiles a chain of effects (turbulence, displacement, kaleidoscope, duotone) into a single fragment shader and runs it on any video, image or canvas source. Here a live 2D canvas of scrolling type is fed in as the 'video', bent by simplex turbulence and recolored through switchable two-ink palettes, all from about ten lines of setup.

name: Metal FX
capabilities: Wrap any button, chip or icon and Metal FX paints an animated liquid-metal rim on it (Paper Shaders' liquidMetal shader), plus metal-filled text, a chrome 'New' badge, mirrored reflections on nearby elements and a cursor-driven liquid dent. Every instance shares one WebGL context and one 15 fps loop, so a whole panel of chrome controls costs about as much as one.

name: Butterchurn
capabilities: Butterchurn runs original MilkDrop .milk presets (per-frame equations, warp and composite shaders) on WebGL, so decades of community feedback-loop art plays in a canvas. This demo cycles 16 curated liquid and chrome presets with blend transitions, fed by a synthesized loop: muted byte data until you tap sound on, or your microphone.

name: regl
capabilities: regl turns WebGL into plain functions: a framebuffer pair and two draw commands give you a ping-pong video-feedback loop in a few lines. Each frame displaces the previous one along curl noise and your pointer, runs a convolution kernel, hue-rotates it, then lights the result as a thin-film oil slick. Built in the spirit of Ezra Miller's iridescentpuddle.com.

name: shader-doodle
capabilities: shader-doodle lets you write fragment shaders as HTML: <sd-node prevbuffer> gives a feedback buffer, <sd-audio> turns an <audio> element into a spectrum + waveform texture, and <sd-uniform> exposes values you set with attributes. Here a polar spectrum ring zooms back into its own trail, running on a procedural spectrum until sound is on.

name: three.js
capabilities: MeshPhysicalMaterial models thin-film interference directly: iridescence, iridescenceIOR and a thickness range (optionally a thickness map) give soap films, holographic foil and nacre without custom shaders. The studio here is three's RoomEnvironment plus coloured softboxes, so the film has hues to shift as you orbit. The slider sets film thickness in nanometres.

name: wavesurfer.js
capabilities: wavesurfer.js renders audio as styled waveforms (gradient bars, rounded caps, split stereo) and adds editing through plugins: draggable regions, a minimap, a timeline and a hover cursor. The 16-bar track is synthesized in WebAudio and handed over as a WAV blob with precomputed peaks. Click a region to loop it, or drag on the wave to cut a new one.

name: glitch-canvas
capabilities: glitch-canvas does not fake glitches with filters: it encodes the image as JPEG, overwrites bytes in the compressed stream (amount, iterations, seed, quality), and decodes whatever survives. You get real DCT block smears and colour-plane shifts. A procedural test-card frame is re-corrupted about 11 times a second, with pointer position setting how hard.

name: VEDA.js
capabilities: VEDA.js, the engine behind the VEDA live-coding VJ tool, runs multipass fragment shaders with named feedback targets and can also synthesize audio from a GLSL mainSound(). The same Lissajous function is used for both: the stereo signal you hear is the X/Y figure on the phosphor scope, with ratios stepping 1:2, 3:2, 5:4, 4:3.

name: woscope
capabilities: woscope draws each audio sample as a beam segment with a Gaussian brightness profile, plus a mipmapped bloom pass, so fast moves fade and slow ones burn in like real phosphor. Here a stereo signal generated in JS (left = X, right = Y) draws a 4D tesseract, a torus knot and stroke text; drag to rotate them, or turn the sound on to hear the picture.

name: Webvs
capabilities: Webvs runs AVS-style presets — JSON chains of SuperScope, DynamicMovement, FadeOut, ColorMap and Mirror components scripted in AVS's EEL expression language, compiled to JS and GLSL. You get the crisp feedback-loop look of late-90s Winamp visuals (warped trails, mirrored scopes, palette-mapped smoke) driven by your own WebAudio source.

name: DSSSP
capabilities: DSSSP brings desktop-plugin EQ UI to React: a log-frequency SVG graph, draggable biquad FilterPoints (drag for freq/gain, wheel for Q), per-filter curves with gradient fills and a summed CompositeCurve. Its exported biquad math also drives this demo's spectrum, and every band mirrors a real Web Audio BiquadFilterNode, so what you drag is what you hear.

name: SiriWave
capabilities: SiriWave recreates both Siri looks on a plain 2D canvas: the iOS 9 multicolour blobs that blend additively and fade in and out, and the thin iOS 7 lines. Feed it amplitude and speed each frame and it eases between values, so a speech rhythm or an audio level meter becomes a convincing assistant UI in a few lines.

name: Audio Borealis
capabilities: The listening glow from the Subtitles Mac app, released as a package: seven soft lobes and five translucent hills, one for each band of the voice, rise from an element's bottom edge and slide sideways while someone talks. It paints with plain 2D canvas under the element's content and has no dependencies. You can drive it from a built-in mock voice, an AnalyserNode, the microphone, or your own levels.

name: html-midi-player
capabilities: <midi-player> and <midi-visualizer> wrap Magenta.js in two HTML tags. The visualizers draw plain SVG rects in light DOM with data-pitch/data-instrument attributes and a --midi-velocity custom property, so ordinary CSS can restyle every note, and the player bar has ::part() hooks. Here one hand-encoded NoteSequence drives all three visualizer types, and a grand staff is built from two instrument-filtered staff views.

name: gpu-io
capabilities: Amanda Ghassaei's gpu-io wraps WebGL1/2 in layers and fragment-shader programs, so a simulation is a few step() calls instead of framebuffer plumbing. Here 128k–1.2M agents (scaled to the GPU) sense, turn and deposit chemoattractant in float textures, building a living transport network you can lure or scatter with the cursor.

name: three-plotter-renderer
capabilities: Renders a three.js scene to a layered SVG built for pen plotters and laser cutters: CPU hidden-line removal keeps only the visible edges, and a GPU normal-buffer pass turns each facet into perspective hatching whose density follows the light. Here a torus knot, a primitive totem and a little city re-plot every frame as two-pen line art; Plot replays the actual stroke order and SVG ↓ saves the file.

name: Heerich
capabilities: meodai's Heerich builds voxel scenes with boolean ops (union, subtract, intersect, exclude) and paints every face from a style map, including the walls a subtraction exposes, then outputs plain SVG polygons with no canvas or WebGL. This sculpture after Erwin Heerich can be carved, drilled and added to by tapping faces (hit-tested with findByPosition). It switches live between oblique, isometric, orthographic and perspective cameras, and three palettes restyle every face.

name: Leon Sans
capabilities: Jongmin Kim's Leon Sans has no font file. Every glyph is stored as stroke coordinates, so canvas code can change the weight smoothly from 1 to 900, draw the letters stroke by stroke, or turn them into waves, patterns and plants. This playground runs the library's own effects (drawing, wave(), pattern(), the colour-pattern example) on any text you type. A plants mode grows leaves along the glyph paths.

name: bouffont
capabilities: bouffont reduces every glyph of a font to its centre lines, redraws them with one pen, then grows them with a chain of strategies: inflate, block, pack, coral or DLA growth, plus outer bands, shine and 3D effects. Every part is tagged with data-part, so this demo styles the plain black-and-white output into graffiti with CSS alone (gradient fills, band colour, stepped drop shadows) and plays bouffontLive() step by step so each piece visibly grows. It's seeded and deterministic, and the letters are Rubik (OFL), loaded from a local WOFF.

name: Heptapod Ink
capabilities: Heptapod Ink packs a phrase into one large number with a CRC-16 checksum and draws each digit as a swelling or tendril on a single brush-ink ring, as plain SVG. The demo reveals each ring clockwise from its gap, eases the library's own displacement filter from wet to settled, then runs decode() on the SVG markup in the DOM and types the text back. Tapping the ring changes the seed: the ink looks different, but it decodes to the same message.

name: Two.js
capabilities: Two.js keeps one scene graph and draws it with an SVG, Canvas 2D or WebGL renderer, so you can switch output without touching drawing code. This grid poster is rebuilt live by whichever renderer you pick: arcs, pills and rings snap on a beat, tiles are clipped with Two.js masks, and hover/drag use its built-in getShapesAtPoint hit-testing.

name: canvas-sketch
capabilities: canvas-sketch works in physical units: you ask for an A4 sheet in millimetres at 300 ppi, and it sizes, scales and animates the canvas for you. Its companion canvas-sketch-util adds seeded random/simplex noise and penplot, which writes the same polylines out as a plotter-ready SVG. This card plots evenly spaced streamlines through seeded noise. You can reseed it, and the SVG export is ready for an AxiDraw.

name: @thi.ng/geom-fuzz
capabilities: Karsten Schmidt's geom-fuzz turns clean @thi.ng/geom shapes into wobbly, overshooting pen strokes, and its fills (hatch, dots, marker-pen) compose like functions, so one compFill() call stacks crosshatch layers. Here a seeded isometric town is shaded face by face with six pen presets built only from those primitives. The outlines 'boil' by cycling a few fresh jitter passes, the way hand-drawn animation does.

name: svg2roughjs
capabilities: Most hand-drawn chart libraries ask you to draw with their API. svg2roughjs takes an SVG you already have and re-renders every element through Rough.js: paths, text, axes, icons. Here a normal D3 dashboard (grouped bars, a spline, a donut, an icon and an annotation) runs crisp under a wipe slider with its sketched copy, which re-sketches about 7 times a second while D3 transitions the data. You can change roughness, fill style, the pencil filter and the seed.

name: Shan Shui (shan-shui-inf)
capabilities: Lingdong Huang's generator paints mountains, pines, pavilions, boats and the odd power pylon from Perlin noise and polylines. It plans and draws every 512-unit stretch of the scroll from a seed. This demo runs the original 2018 scripts unmodified: it asks for new chunks as you unroll, rasterises each window once and pans it, and the white occluder fills vanish into the paper through a multiply blend as on the original page.
installs: git clone https://github.com/LingDong-/shan-shui-inf (not on npm; vendor the inline scripts)

name: Penrose
capabilities: CMU's Penrose splits a diagram into Domain (types), Substance (what is true) and Style (how to draw it), then finds a layout by numerically minimising constraint energy. Here you edit the Substance live and watch the optimizer's real trajectory replayed, with the energy curve drawn alongside. Drag a set and Penrose solves again from where you dropped it.

name: MarkovJunior Web
capabilities: Yuu6883's browser port of mxgmn's MarkovJunior (MIT), a language where a program is an XML tree of pattern rewrites like WBB → WAW, applied at random until nothing matches. Eight models from the repo (rivers, flowers, dungeons, islands, a lost city) grow on the real interpreter here. The node that is firing is lit up in its XML source, and its in → out patterns are drawn in the model's palette.

name: Krbn
capabilities: Krbn draws strokes rather than shading pixels. Silhouettes of spheres, cones and cylinders come out as exact conics, hidden edges are split analytically into ghosted runs, and the hatching follows each surface's own curvature. Every frame here is a new SVG from a live orbit camera. A FrameSession keys the hand-drawn wobble to stable stroke identities, so the lines slide as you orbit instead of boiling.

name: Spectral.js
capabilities: Spectral.js turns each colour into a reflectance curve and mixes the curves with Kubelka-Munk theory, so blue and yellow make green the way paint does instead of averaging to grey. The demo is a smudgy brush simulation. One painting is rendered twice, spectral on one side of the slider and plain RGB averaging on the other, so the same strokes show both results.

name: p5.grain
capabilities: p5.grain applies the analog finish that generative prints usually get in post: per-pixel monochromatic or chromatic grain, tiled paper textures blended onto the canvas, and a tinkerPixels loop for custom pixel passes. Here a three-ink riso poster runs through all three on a sheet-sized p5.Graphics buffer, using a seeded random so the grain is deterministic. Drag the wipe to compare it with the clean render.

name: Poline
capabilities: meodai's Poline puts colours on a polar wheel, with hue as the angle and lightness as the radius, then interpolates between anchor points. A separate position function eases each axis, so the same anchors give very different ramps under sinusoidal, exponential or arc. This demo uses Poline's own <poline-picker> web component: drag the anchors and the Bauhaus tile poster and swatch strip recolour live. The hue drifts slowly when idle.

name: Sketchy Plants
capabilities: Orta Therox's generator grows 52 species from a seed and draws them with broken hand-length pen strokes, off-register watercolour washes and paper knockouts, returning a plain SVG string with no DOM and no dependencies. Age is not a scale factor: as it rises, leaf count, fenestration, crown spread and pot wear all change, so the growth animation here shows a monstera's blades splitting as it matures. Tap a pot to sow a new seed, or swap the palette and the paper changes with it.

name: hairline
capabilities: Each figure is a filled-plate isometric line drawing (a keyboard, a vault, a commit graph) that does one physical thing when the pointer arrives: a key sinks, a dial turns, a drawer slides out. All 33 share one requestAnimationFrame loop, are themed with five CSS custom properties, and each reports a live caption such as 'lid 112°'. This sheet pages through every figure, with the library's own ghost tour running while the page is idle.

name: Globe.gl
capabilities: One chainable component layers animated dashed great-circle arcs, H3 hexbin columns, propagating rings and dotted country polygons on a three.js globe. Here a dotted Natural Earth landmass, metro-population columns and bloom give the night-dashboard look without any map tiles or textures.

name: cosmos.gl
capabilities: Repulsion, link springs and clustering all run in WebGL shaders, so tens of thousands of points simulate live in the browser. This galaxy is 48,000 points and ~70k links held in spiral arms by cluster forces; explode it and watch the GPU pull it back together.

name: deck.gl
capabilities: deck.gl renders data as composable WebGL layers that do not depend on a basemap. A generated street grid, 900 TripsLayer trails with fading tails and additive blending, and a HexagonLayer aggregating pickups into extruded towers make a city portrait with no map tiles.

name: 3d-force-graph
capabilities: A force-directed graph in true 3D with directional link particles, curved links and access to the three.js post-processing composer. Nine scale-free 'lobes' joined by curved axons stream particles under an UnrealBloom pass; clicking a node flies the camera to it.

name: Sigma.js
capabilities: Sigma draws graphology graphs in WebGL, and v4 adds declarative, state-driven styles (whenState, hasHighlighted) in place of hand-written reducers. The graph here is this lane's own npm dependency tree from package-lock.json, coloured by Louvain community and laid out by ForceAtlas2 in a web worker.

name: textures.js
capabilities: textures.js generates SVG <pattern> fills (hatching, dots, waves, hexagons) that you apply to any shape with .url(). The fills replace colour in this two-ink, risograph-style world map and bar legend, so the classes still read in greyscale print. Data: Natural Earth (public domain).

name: d3-voronoi-treemap
capabilities: Instead of rectangles, cells are weighted Voronoi polygons inside any convex shape, which gives hierarchical data an organic, cell-like look. Countries nest inside continents within a circle, and the cells morph between GDP (PPP) and population shares. Data: Natural Earth (public domain).

name: d3-geo-projection
capabilities: d3-geo-projection exposes each projection's raw math, so you can write a raw function that blends two of them and morph the world from Hammer to Larrivée to Bertin 1953. Paired with d3-geo-polygon's clipped polyhedral projections (Cahill–Keyes, Waterman, Fuller's Airocean), the same canvas path renders Tissot's indicatrices that show each projection's distortion. Natural Earth 110m land (public domain) via world-atlas.

name: webgl-wind
capabilities: Vladimir Agafonkin's webgl-wind keeps every particle position in a texture and advects it in a fragment shader against a u/v wind PNG, so 65k trails cost the CPU nothing. The fading screen-texture feedback gives the streaks their silky ink look; here it runs on real NOAA GFS frames (public domain) with a custom teal-to-ember speed ramp.

name: mapgen4
capabilities: mapgen4 builds a Delaunay/Voronoi dual mesh, runs elevation, wind-driven rainfall and river flow in a Web Worker, then renders it with an oblique projection and outline shading that reads like a hand-drawn relief map. Paint ocean, valleys or peaks and the rivers, biomes and rain shadows recompute in tens of milliseconds.

name: d3-graphviz
capabilities: d3-graphviz runs real Graphviz (compiled to WebAssembly) in the browser, then diffs each new layout against the last and tweens nodes, edges and shapes between them. You write plain DOT strings per state and get morphing diagrams without placing a single coordinate yourself. Here nine DOT keyframes of a git repo branch, merge and squash; the layout flips TB/LR with the viewport.

name: MathBox
capabilities: Steven Wittens' declarative scene graph for math diagrams: emit data with expr callbacks, then draw it as surfaces, vectors, lines and SDF labels with crisp, resolution-independent strokes. Here |f(z)| becomes a domain-colored relief that morphs between z², z³−1, sin z and 1/z while particle trails ride the field.

name: ENCOM Globe
capabilities: Rob Scanlon's recreation of the ENCOM boardroom globe: continents built from hexasphere tiles that sweep in with a build-up animation, spring-loaded pins, orange markers joined by arcs, and satellites pulsing wave rings. A distinct film-UI look next to generic globe libraries.

name: Rough.js
capabilities: Rough.js turns any rectangle, ellipse, polygon or SVG path into wobbly, hand-drawn strokes with hachure, cross-hatch, zigzag or dot fills. A seed makes each sketch reproducible, so cycling through three seeds gives the 'line boil' of hand-drawn animation. At under 9 kB gzipped, it powers Excalidraw-style UIs and wired-elements.

name: Wired Elements
capabilities: Wired Elements is a set of Lit web components (buttons, inputs, combos, sliders, toggles, progress bars) drawn with Rough.js. Each control re-sketches itself at its real pixel size, so no two renders are identical. They work in any framework or none, and are useful for prototypes that should look unfinished.

name: chart.xkcd
capabilities: chart.xkcd draws charts the way Randall Munroe does: jittery axes, the xkcd handwriting font (embedded in the bundle) and boxed tooltips that follow the cursor. It has six chart types behind a Chart.js-like config with no dependencies, and supports custom stroke and background colours for dark themes.

name: roughViz
capabilities: roughViz is a set of D3 charts (bar, donut, line, scatter, stacked) rendered with Rough.js, so fills come out as hachure, zigzag or dot patterns and outlines wobble. Fill style and roughness are plain options, and redrawing the chart re-sketches it, which this demo uses for an idle shimmer. Good for data that should feel informal or approximate.

name: perfect-freehand
capabilities: perfect-freehand takes raw pointer samples and returns the outline polygon of a variable-width stroke, simulating pressure from speed when there is no stylus. Thinning, smoothing, streamline and taper are numbers you can tune live. It powers the ink in tldraw and Excalidraw-style apps, and you render the output yourself as SVG or canvas paths.

name: Excalidraw
capabilities: @excalidraw/excalidraw is the full Excalidraw editor packaged as one React component, including its tools, Rough.js shapes and Excalifont handwriting. You can preload a scene from a compact skeleton format, drive it through an imperative API, and serve its fonts yourself instead of from a CDN. Useful for diagrams people should be able to edit in place.

name: Vivus
capabilities: Vivus animates stroke-dashoffset on every path of an inline SVG, so line art appears to be drawn by hand. It has three timing modes (delayed, sync, oneByOne), separate easing per path and for the whole timeline, and setFrameProgress() for scrubbing or scroll-linking. It has no dependencies and works on any SVG you already have.

name: 98.css
capabilities: 98.css styles plain semantic HTML — buttons, fieldsets, tree views, tabs, progress bars — with pixel-exact Win98 bevels and a bundled bitmap MS Sans Serif. No JavaScript and no class soup: a <button> just looks like a Win98 button, so whole desktop UIs come from markup alone.

name: XP.css
capabilities: XP.css extends 98.css with the Luna theme: glossy blue title bars, rounded red close buttons, orange-highlighted tabs and the segmented green progress bar. Same semantic-HTML approach, so swapping eras is mostly a stylesheet change.

name: 7.css
capabilities: 7.css recreates Aero: translucent glass window frames, glowing caption buttons, the shimmering progress bar and balloon tooltips. The frame colour is one CSS custom property (--w7-w-bg), so the demo recolours every window live from a swatch picker.

name: system.css
capabilities: system.css draws the 1-bit Macintosh look: pinstriped title bars, square close boxes, dithered desktop and recreated Chicago and Geneva bitmap fonts. Pure black and white with no anti-aliasing, so it stays crisp at integer zoom.

name: NES.css
capabilities: NES.css turns containers, buttons, progress bars and speech balloons into chunky 8-bit components with stepped pixel borders, and ships pixel-art icons and sprites as pure CSS. Pair it with Press Start 2P and a whole game UI comes out of class names.

name: Webamp
capabilities: Webamp is a full reimplementation of Winamp 2.9: docking main, EQ and playlist windows, a working 10-band equalizer, the visualizer, and support for classic .wsz skins. Here the three tracks are synthesized in the browser with OfflineAudioContext and handed to Webamp as WAV blobs.

name: augmented-ui
capabilities: augmented-ui gives any element sci-fi geometry — clipped and rounded corners, notches, tabs, inset borders — from a single data-augmented-ui attribute, sized by CSS custom properties. No SVG and no extra DOM, so the panels stay responsive and animatable.

name: WebTUI
capabilities: WebTUI lays out the web on a monospace character grid: box-drawing borders, badges, progress bars and tables align to cells, configured through attribute selectors like box-="round" and is-="badge". Themes such as Catppuccin, Gruvbox and Nord are separate packages switched with one data attribute.

name: cursor-effects
capabilities: cursor-effects revives the GeoCities-era cursor trail: fairy dust, rainbow, ghost, bubbles, a clock and text flags, each drawn on a canvas and attached with one function call. Every effect returns a destroy() handle, so switching between them at runtime is easy.

name: JS Paint
capabilities: JS Paint recreates Windows 98 Paint down to the tool cursors, fill modes and the 28-swatch palette, then adds extras like unlimited undo, themes and image formats. This demo embeds the real app and paints a whole scene with ordinary pointer events: it clicks the toolbox, palette and option choosers like a person would, and stops the moment you start drawing.
installs: git clone https://github.com/1j01/jspaint (static app, serve the folder)

name: OS-GUI
capabilities: OS-GUI (the toolkit behind 98.js.org and JS Paint) themes itself from real Windows .theme INI files at runtime: every [Control Panel\Colors] key becomes a CSS variable and the bevels, checker dithers and scrollbar arrows are regenerated as data URLs. Edit a number in the theme file and the whole UI re-skins, flying-titlebar minimize animation included.

name: WinBox
capabilities: WinBox gives you real draggable, resizable, minimizable windows that hold any DOM node, in about 12 kB with no framework. Its geometry API (move, resize, focus, setBackground) is small enough to build tiling, focus and cascade layouts on top, as this desk does with live canvas widgets inside each window.

name: React95
capabilities: React95 rebuilds the Windows 95 widget kit (bevelled frames, dithered pressed buttons, 7-segment counters, a CRT Monitor) as styled-components that read every color from one theme object. Swap the object and the whole UI re-skins live; nest ThemeProviders and many themes render side by side, as in the scheme list here.

name: TuiCss
capabilities: TuiCss styles ordinary HTML as a 1990s text-mode utility: double-line fieldset frames, the 16-color VGA palette as utility classes like blue-168 and cyan-255-text, hard black drop shadows and a bundled CP437 VGA font. Menus, modals, tabs and block-character progress bars stay semantic HTML.

name: oneko
capabilities: oneko packages the 1989 desktop cat as a tiny engine with bundled sprite coats, naps, thought bubbles, treats, toss-able cats and keep-out zones. With chase: "cat" each cat follows the one mounted before it, so a few instances form a parade; here an idle ghost pointer keeps them moving and touch input is bridged for phones.

name: Classic Stylesheets
capabilities: One package styles plain HTML as Windows 3.x, 9x/2000, XP, CDE or Mac OS 9, and its 205 skins recolor each theme through CSS variables. This desktop never re-renders: a Notepad, a list view and a tabbed Display Properties dialog switch eras by swapping a single <style> tag. The windows drag and maximize through the library's own wm.js module.

name: Aqua
capabilities: Lickable gel buttons, barber-pole progress bars, pinstriped windows, a Dock and a click-wheel music player, shipped as copy-in shadcn components on Radix + Tailwind. One --aqua-accent variable drives every gel gradient via color-mix, so recoloring the whole skin is a single CSS change.
installs: npx shadcn@latest add https://aqua.duca.dev/r/theme.json https://aqua.duca.dev/r/button.json https://aqua.duca.dev/r/dock.json

name: PSone.css
capabilities: PSone.css recreates late-90s console menus: navy gradient windows with a double white bevel, gradient-fade buttons, segmented HP/MP-style progress bars and radio options picked by a pointer cursor. Here it runs a two-slot memory-card manager with original save icons, a party status preview and a copy/delete confirm dialog.

name: TheSims.css
capabilities: A classless kit (adapted from 98.css) that restyles native buttons, skewed buttons, radios, checkboxes, range sliders and scrollbars as the chunky navy bevel panels and Comic-font controls of a 2000 life-sim. The demo drives decaying needs bars, a game clock on speed radios, an action queue, a buy catalog and an isometric build preview.

name: YoRHa CSS
capabilities: YoRHa styles plain HTML (h1, figure/figcaption, table, blockquote, button) as a khaki field terminal on a hairline grid, with no classes needed. Its signature move is the button highlight: an inverted bar slides in from the left between two hairlines. Here a build-time transform copies every :hover rule to an .is-hover class, so the library's own CSS draws the idle auto-cursor and the keyboard cursor.

name: Frutiger.js
capabilities: A pure-CSS (cascade-layered) design system plus React wrappers that rebuilds the mid-2000s Frutiger Aero look: gel pill buttons, specular gloss caps, acrylic window frames and Vista-style taskbars. It also ships canvas effects like a swaying GrassField, rising AeroBackgroundFX bubbles and a WaterRipple that splashes wherever you tap.

name: A E S T H E T I C
capabilities: A small Sass/CSS framework that mixes Windows 95 and XP chrome (modals, tabs, taskbar, boot loaders, notifications) with a seapunk pink, lilac and cyan palette. Its effects layer adds a CRT scanline-and-flicker overlay and an attr()-driven text glitch, so a whole page reads as a late-night mall broadcast.

name: BOOTSTRA.386
capabilities: BOOTSTRA.386 re-skins stock Bootstrap 5 into an EGA 16-colour, 16px-cell text-mode screen: blue background, square corners, one fixed font size for every element. Unmodified navbar, card, table, list-group, progress, badge, input-group and a real Bootstrap Modal make up this fictional BBS, so ordinary Bootstrap markup turns into a 386-era terminal.

name: 3GS UI
capabilities: A React design system that rebuilds 2009-era handset chrome from CSS alone: half-split gel gradients, pinstripe grouped tables, ON/OFF pill switches, pointed back buttons and lucide icons tinted through an SVG gloss gradient. Every colour and gel is a --gs-* token, with a dark default and the blue-gray light theme one attribute away.

name: Retrostrap
