capabilities: A zero-dependency CSS + JS kit that enforces the era: web-safe colors only, nine period font stacks, radius 0, hard bevels, linear motion. Marquees, odometer hit counters, webrings, guestbooks and LED clocks are real widgets, and Retrostrap.audit() flags anything that slips out of 1999.

name: LCARS CSS
capabilities: A class-based CSS framework (no JS) for the elbow-frame console look: elbows, segmented bars, pill elements, hollow brackets, blinking text boxes, row-scanning tables and a large named colour palette, all sized on a rem grid. Because everything is rem-based, the whole console rescales from one root font size, and switching colour classes recolours the full frame.

name: Arwes
capabilities: Arwes builds interfaces out of SVG frames that draw their own outlines, text that deciphers into place and canvas grids, dots and moving lines, all timed by one Animator tree so panels enter in staggered sequence. It also ships a bleeps manager for UI sounds; here every bleep is synthesized in the browser into WAV blobs, so the demo bundles no audio files.

name: cyberpunk-css
capabilities: One stylesheet of acid-yellow, cyan and red components cut from clip-path polygons: notched buttons with a glitch layer, chamfered tiles, razor-edged borders, striped banners and five keyframe glitch effects. It needs no JavaScript and no build step. Every panel, table, checkbox, input, banner meter and dialog here is a stock class; the upstream BlenderPro and logo fonts aren't redistributable, so they're aliased to OFL Rajdhani and Oxanium.

name: CYBERCORE CSS
capabilities: A zero-JS design system built on CSS layers, color-mix() and custom properties: chamfered cards with bracket corners, glitch text driven by a data-text attribute, scanline and datastream overlays, striped and segmented meters, terminals, alerts and tables. Retheme it by overriding its --cyber-* and --space-* tokens; the optional icon registry renders SVG strings for the same palette.

name: Frontpanel
capabilities: Frontpanel gives you .fp-* classes and --fp-* tokens for building device front panels: liquid-chrome rims, gel pills, molded caps, LCD glass with ghost segments, seven-segment readouts, LED meters, knobs and faders. Everything sits in one cascade layer, so your own CSS wins, and a data-fp-skin attribute flips the whole device between Chrome Silver and Gunmetal Night.

name: PaperCSS
capabilities: PaperCSS gets its sketchy look from pure CSS: asymmetric elliptical border-radius values make every border wobble, and plain classes like paper-btn, badge, alert, progress and tabs restyle native HTML. No JS runtime and no images, so the hand-drawn look survives zooming and theming.

name: Doodle CSS
capabilities: Doodle CSS draws its boxes, buttons, checkboxes, radios, hr and blockquote with border-image slices of hand-drawn SVGs, so plain form markup inside a .doodle wrapper looks scribbled. The demo inverts the ink with a CSS filter to turn the same SVGs into chalk and blueprint themes.

name: React Pixel UI
capabilities: <Pixel> reads an element's computed border-radius, border, gradient and box-shadow and redraws them as staircase clip-paths, block-sampled gradient PNGs and hard drop-shadows, with no canvas. Your existing CSS stays the source of truth: change a class or style and the pixel version is regenerated, including the shimmering pedestal gradient in this demo.

name: CSS Houdini Ring Particles
capabilities: Bramus's worklet behind the Google I/O 2022 hero: every dot is drawn by paint(ring-particles), and the only animation is a registered --animation-tick custom property going 0 → 1. Three stacked layers with different seeds, lags and blend modes trail the pointer through @property transitions on --ring-x/--ring-y. Non-Chromium browsers get the same worklet through css-paint-polyfill.

name: Houdini Doom Fire
capabilities: registerPaint('doomfire') runs the classic PSX Doom fire cellular automaton inside paint(), so any background, even background-clip: text letters, can burn; animating one registered length makes it repaint every frame. Here it rises from a horizon drawn by the same author's houdini-sunset worklet (gradient sky + pixel perspective grid), all from CSS.

name: CSS Houdini Voronoi
capabilities: registerPaint('voronoi') turns a handful of custom properties (cell count, margin, line and dot colours, seed) into a background-image, and its seeded sites make the diagram deterministic. Here a second layer with the same seed at 2× size is clipped into a lens and lines up exactly with the tissue beneath it, while both layers breathe on one @property-animated --voronoi-margin. The out-of-focus debris comes from its sibling worklet, css-houdini-circles.

name: CSS Houdini Fractals
capabilities: One registerPaint('fractals') worklet draws a recursive binary tree of lines, circles or squares from the element's bottom edge, styled entirely by custom properties: --angle, --next-line-size, --shape and a space-separated --colors list it cycles per segment. Here three trees share the worklet; a registered <integer> --angle is computed from an @property --sway keyframe, so the grove sways without any JS animation loop.

name: Houdini Cosmic Starfield
capabilities: Stephanie Eckles's worklet paints a gradient sky, stars and optional cosmic clouds from three custom properties, and the star count doubles as the PRNG seed, so one number is a whole reproducible sky. Here it is stacked as transparent star-only layers (8-digit #00000000 gradient), SVG-tinted nebula bands and a dust lane, all drifting and parallaxing on the compositor, and a warp swaps every seed.

name: Houdini Tesla & Noise
capabilities: Two tiny paint worklets: tesla-coil strokes a fresh random jagged arc with a shadowBlur glow every time an input changes, and noise fills a box with random HSL cells. Here three stacked arc strips are rotated and stretched between two electrodes, re-randomised by a stepped @property keyframe, while noise textures the console deck, the buttons and a tiled film grain.

name: Extra.css
capabilities: Five tiny CSS Paint API worklets (confetti, sparkles, scalloped border, super-underline, cross-out) that you drive entirely from custom properties in your stylesheet. Here every decoration is a background-image: paint(); the random worklets re-roll whenever an input property changes, so a steps() keyframe on a registered property gives them a hand-drawn stop-motion boil.

name: Motion
capabilities: Motion's vanilla animate() drives real spring physics through hardware-accelerated transforms, and re-targeting a running spring keeps its velocity, so a tile pushed mid-bounce never snaps. Function-valued delays and stagger() turn one call into a grid-wide ripple; press() adds tactile gestures without a framework.

name: GSAP
capabilities: Flip records element positions, lets you mutate the DOM however you like (swap classes, reorder children), then animates from the old layout to the new one, even between CSS grid templates. Draggable with InertiaPlugin adds momentum throws and edge resistance, so cards can be thrown, dropped on each other to swap, and spring back.

name: anime.js
capabilities: anime.js v4's stagger() understands 2D grids: give it the column/row count and an origin index and every property delay, offset and value radiates outward from that cell. Tween keyframes with per-step easings (outElastic, outBounce) and the built-in splitText make choreographed type and grid motion a few declarative objects.

name: Matter.js
capabilities: Matter.js handles collisions, friction, restitution, sleeping bodies and mouse constraints, and leaves rendering to you, so physics can look like type and UI instead of debug wireframes. Here every letter and pill is a chamfered rigid body drawn on a custom canvas renderer.

name: Lenis
capabilities: Lenis interpolates the wheel/trackpad input while the page keeps its real scrollbar, position: sticky and anchor links. Its scroll event exposes eased scroll, velocity and progress every frame, enough to drive parallax layers, velocity-skewed marquees and progress bars from one listener.

name: Atropos
capabilities: Atropos tilts a card toward the pointer and shifts each child by its data-atropos-offset, so stacked layers read as real depth, with a moving highlight and a soft shadow. It is markup-driven (no canvas, no WebGL), so the scene stays plain HTML, SVG and CSS.

name: AutoAnimate
capabilities: One call on a parent element and every child insert, removal and reorder animates with a FLIP transition; there is no animation code anywhere else in this demo. It works with plain DOM or any framework (React, Vue, Svelte, Angular hooks), which makes it a cheap upgrade for lists, tables and menus.

name: canvas-confetti
capabilities: A single function call launches physically tumbling paper with spread, gravity, drift, decay and flat/3D flutter. Custom shapes come from SVG paths or text glyphs via shapeFromPath and shapeFromText, and confetti.create() binds it to your own canvas.

name: Tweakpane
capabilities: Tweakpane binds controls directly to a plain object: numbers become sliders, hex strings become color pickers, {x, y} becomes a 2D pad, and readonly bindings become live graphs. It is themed entirely through CSS custom properties, which makes it a good-looking default for creative-coding and debug panels.

name: Kinesis 2
capabilities: Kinesis turns registered CSS variables like --k-tilt, --k-magnetic or --k-look into spring-animated pointer behaviour, so motion lives in your stylesheet next to colour and spacing. It writes only translate/rotate/scale, works through media queries and calc(), and runs one shared loop that stops when nothing moves. Here one postcard combines tilt + depth layers, a magnetic dock, repelling stars, a following paper plane and a bird that looks at you.

name: flubber
capabilities: flubber morphs between shapes with different point counts and topology: it resamples both outlines, finds the best rotation to align them, and triangulates a shape to split it into many (separate) or fuse many into one (combine). Here a fish breaks into a school of seven, the school merges into a bird, and a moon scatters into stars. Each step is a plain t → path function driven by a hand-rolled rAF tween.

name: KUTE.js
capabilities: KUTE.js tweens things CSS can't: svgCubicMorph converts two unrelated paths to cubic béziers, splits them to equal segment counts and picks the rotation with the least travel, svgDraw animates stroke length, and textWrite scrambles text into place character by character. Here a chain of seven glyphs morphs with lagging outline echoes, a drawn progress ring, a type-written label and a matrix-based 3D sway, all as plain KUTE tweens from its 'extra' build.

name: React Flip Toolkit
capabilities: Wrap elements in Flipped, change a flipKey, and the toolkit measures before and after, then plays the difference on a real spring (Rebound fork) instead of a CSS easing. The Stripe-style dropdown is one background morphing between panels with an inverseFlipId child cancelling its scale; each card opens with its own stiffness/damping, children staggered, and the standalone spring() drives the replay ball.

name: React Bubble UI
capabilities: A scrollable hex grid where every bubble scales by its distance from the viewport centre, with a fringe band that shrinks and gravitates items into the edges. Here it runs a 38-app watch face of hand-drawn SVG glyphs that drifts on its own; provideProps feeds each bubble its live size so icons fade as they shrink.

name: Scene.js + Timeline
capabilities: Scene.js describes animation as plain data: time-keyed keyframe objects per element, with selector items that fan out into staggered sub-items via per-index delays. The companion @scenejs/timeline docks an After-Effects-style panel that reads the same scene, so every keyframe, delay bar and playhead is inspectable and scrubbable live.

name: Shuffle.js
capabilities: Shuffle.js packs items into columns and animates them to new spots with CSS transforms when you filter or sort. It's an MIT alternative to Isotope with sort functions, per-item stagger and filter callbacks. 44 historical pigments re-sort by hue, lightness, chroma or closeness to a tapped colour, and the tiles resize so whatever is left fills the wall.

name: Disintegrate
capabilities: Disintegrate screenshots real DOM nodes with html2canvas and turns their pixels into canvas particles, so the dust carries the element's actual text and icon colours. It can burst a whole element at once or emit particles only where an element slides past its container edge, and particle behaviour is a pluggable constructor. Here two built-in types sit next to two custom ones registered with addParticleType.

name: Motion Canvas
capabilities: Scenes are TypeScript generators: every yield* is a tween, and nodes bind straight to reactive signals, so labels and diagrams update with the values they show. Its Code node morphs one snippet into the next token by token, which is what makes its 3Blue1Brown-style explainers look the way they do.

name: interact.js
capabilities: interact.js gives you raw pointer physics rather than a drag-and-drop widget: throws keep their momentum and glide to a stop, modifiers snap to a grid or clamp to the parent, and two-finger gestures report rotation and scale. It only reports deltas and leaves rendering to you, so the transforms here are plain CSS variables.

name: Shopify Draggable
capabilities: Shopify's Draggable splits drag and drop into sensors, a mirror and behaviours (Swappable, Sortable, Droppable), with plugins such as SwapAnimation and SortAnimation for the FLIP motion. Here Swappable runs a poster puzzle and Sortable reorders the layers that redraw the poster; when idle, a ghost cursor drives the real mouse sensor.

name: Muuri
capabilities: Muuri packs variable-size items into a masonry layout and animates every reflow, whether it comes from a drag, a filter, a sort or an item moving between grids. Grids connect through dragSort, so cards can cross boards with a spring-eased release while both layouts repack.

name: AnimXYZ
capabilities: AnimXYZ builds animations from words: an xyz="fade small rotate-right stagger-0.5" attribute sets CSS variables, and a single shared keyframe combines them, so effects stack without writing @keyframes. Stagger reads a per-element --xyz-index, which drives the diagonal sweep here. Toggle the chips to mix your own.

name: Animata
capabilities: Animata is a shadcn-style registry of animated React components: you copy the source (or pull it with the shadcn CLI) and own it, styled with Tailwind v4 and driven by Motion or plain CSS keyframes. This board runs ten of its text effects verbatim (gibberish scramble, odometer ticker, spring counter, RGB glitch, blur wave reveal, typing, split, swap, roll, mirror), each auto-replaying on its own timer.

name: Theme Toggles
capabilities: Alfie Jones' toggles are small SVG pieces where the sun becomes a moon through clip-path and path-d morphs, eclipses and expanding rays, all driven by CSS transitions with no JS animation. Each one is a <button> with a toggled prop and a duration knob, and works with a .dark class on the root.

name: Hamburgers
capabilities: Jonathan Suh's Hamburgers turns the three-line menu icon into 31 ways to become an X or an arrow (3D flips, elastic, spring, squeeze, vortex), using only pseudo-elements and transforms on one .is-active class. The markup is three spans; colour and size come from CSS or the Sass variables.

name: Rive
capabilities: Rive files carry their own state machines: number, boolean and trigger inputs plus pointer listeners, all authored in the editor and run by a small WASM runtime on a canvas. This stage lists each machine's live inputs as sliders, toggles and trigger chips, and streams state changes and Rive events to a log. Example .riv files © Rive, MIT, from rive-app/rive-wasm.

name: dotLottie Web
capabilities: dotLottie packages Lottie JSON with themes and interactive state machines into one zipped .lottie file, rendered by a ThorVG WebAssembly engine. This orbit animation, its four colour themes and its hover/tap state machine are all written in code and zipped in the browser. Colour slots let one file re-skin with setTheme(), and named markers drive each state.

name: Flicking
capabilities: A circular coverflow of ten procedurally drawn typographic posters, built entirely from Flicking's official plugins: Perspective tilts and scales each panel by its outset progress, Parallax slides the artwork under the type, Fade dims captions, and AutoPlay, Arrow and Pagination handle navigation. One panel-progress model drives every effect, so drag, flick and autoplay stay in sync.

name: smooothy
capabilities: smooothy is a small lerped slider core: you call update() in your own loop and read current, parallaxValues and deltaTime to build the effects yourself. Here the measured speed is smoothed with its own damp() and drives skew, squash, a colour trail and a background marquee across twelve canvas-painted landscapes, with idle auto-drift surges so it never stands still.

name: Interior
capabilities: Interior covers the half-second after a click: hold-to-confirm that unwinds at 2.5× when released, optimistic likes that batch rapid taps into one request, and buttons whose labels swap without layout shift. Each item is one copy-in Motion component with reduced-motion, ARIA and keyboard handling built in.

The slider snaps to labelled stops within a capture radius and vibrates once per crossing on phones. The segmented control's sliding thumb inverts the label it passes over, and presets visibly sink when pressed. Spring-tuned Motion components you copy into your codebase and own.

name: React Wheel Picker
capabilities: An unstyled React wheel picker that renders options on a real rotateX cylinder, with flick inertia, infinite looping, mouse-wheel and keyboard support. Three linked drums (hour, minute, AM/PM) drive a live 'rings in' countdown and a 24h arc, and the idle spin sends real flick gestures so the library's own inertia does the motion.

name: animate-css-grid
capabilities: One wrapGrid() call makes CSS grid changes animate with transforms: column count, spans and DOM order. It counter-scales each tile's single child so content isn't distorted mid-flight. This glyph-specimen mosaic trades a 2×2 hero span between tiles, reflows between 4/6/8 columns and shuffles with backOut springing and stagger.

name: Parallax.js
capabilities: Wagerfield's classic engine moves each child of a scene by its data-depth, using the device gyroscope on phones and the cursor elsewhere. Eight procedurally cut SVG sheets with paper grain, lit top edges and stacked drop shadows turn it into a shadow-box diorama, and an idle drift feeds the library simulated cursor input.

name: mo.js
capabilities: mo.js ships SVG motion primitives (Shape, ShapeSwirl, Burst) instead of a generic tween API: you declare a burst of zigzags, crosses and curves with property maps and it choreographs the whole explosion. This garden pools 14 layered bursts and replays them with .tune({x, y}).replay(), so the DOM never grows, around the classic mo.js like-heart burst.

Every mo.js module (Shape, ShapeSwirl, Burst, Html) has its own .then() chain and drops into a mojs.Timeline, so a full logo sting (swirl in, squash, collide, burst, type, settle) is about 150 lines of declarations. The official @mojs/player adds a play/loop/speed bar and a scrubber that seeks the timeline, which makes it useful for tuning motion while you build it.

name: Swiper
capabilities: Swiper ships cube, cards, flip and coverflow transitions plus a 'creative' effect where you describe prev/next slides as translate/rotate/scale/opacity vectors. The same seven procedurally drawn posters are destroyed and re-initialised under each effect, with the live config printed underneath — Fan, Orbit and Hinge are creativeEffect presets.

A full-bleed vertical Swiper where each scene is built from SVG ridge layers tagged with data-swiper-parallax-y, so near hills travel further than the sky during a slide. A custom creativeEffect with progressMultiplier tilts the outgoing scene back into a rounded plate while the next one rises over it.

name: Moveable
capabilities: Moveable wraps any DOM element in a design-tool control box: drag, resize, rotate, a 4-corner perspective warp that writes matrix3d, and a clip-path editor with per-vertex handles. Its snapping draws Figma-style pink guidelines with live distance and gap labels against other elements and the artboard edges, so you get a canvas editor's feel without writing the hit-testing math.

name: SmoothUI
capabilities: SmoothUI is a shadcn registry of Framer Motion components that copy into your repo as source. One AIState value (idle, listening, thinking, streaming, done) drives every AI piece: here it sets the Siri orb's speed, saturation and bloom while the Dynamic Island springs between call, message, music and timer layouts.

Two SmoothUI stack primitives side by side. time-machine-stack recedes panels in real CSS 3D (translateZ, scale, offset, no opacity tricks); card-swipe-deck throws cards along the finger's velocity, with Keep/Skip stamps tied to drag distance. All card art is generated as inline SVG.

name: Tailwind Motion
capabilities: Rombo's plugin turns enter/loop animations into Tailwind utilities: presets like motion-preset-pop or blur-left, plus base classes for translate, scale, rotate, blur and opacity that stack on one element. Spring easings are generated with CSS linear() curves, so springy motion works without any JavaScript runtime. This board shows each class string next to the UI it animates, and lets you compose your own stack.

name: pushIn.js
capabilities: pushIn.js turns page scroll into a camera dolly: stacked layers scale up from the vanishing point and fade out as they pass you, each with its own in/out scroll points, speed and fade lengths. Plain HTML plus data attributes, no WebGL and no framework, so typographic and SVG art stays crisp at any zoom.

name: React Kino
capabilities: Kino pins scenes with position: sticky and hands every child the scene's 0–1 progress, so reveals, counters, 3D ScrollTransforms and word-by-word TextReveal all key off one timeline. It updates DOM styles through progress subscriptions instead of re-rendering React each frame, and ships HorizontalScroll, Parallax, Progress and Marquee in the same package.

name: r3f-scroll-rig
capabilities: 14islands' rig keeps one shared GlobalCanvas behind a normal HTML page: each or div stays in the layout as a proxy while a ScrollScene draws a WebGL mesh at the exact same size and position, synced with Lenis smooth scrolling. Here every artwork is a plain loaded as a texture via useImageAsTexture, rendered as a shader plane that bends, ripples and RGB-splits with scroll velocity from useScrollbar.

name: impress.js
capabilities: impress.js places every slide at a position, rotation and scale in one 3D world, then moves the camera between them with CSS transforms, so the slides never move. Pan, spin, zoom out to a ×3 slide, dive 1800px into the screen or tilt onto the floor, all set with data attributes. Autoplay, keyboard, swipe and click navigation are built-in plugins.

name: SSGOI
capabilities: SSGOI animates page swaps with spring physics on the Web Animations API: hero shared elements, drill-in stacks, tab slides and sheets. Route rules (from/to, on/except, ordered) decide the effect and its forward/backward direction, so it works with any router, or none. This demo routes from React state alone.

name: transition.css
capabilities: transition.css ships circle, square, diamond, polygon and wipe reveals as plain @keyframes animating clip-path, triggered by a single transition-style="in:circle:hesitate" attribute. No JS runtime: set or remove the attribute to fire or re-arm it, and tune timing with --transition__duration / --transition__easing custom properties. Here, twelve procedurally drawn CSS/SVG posters swap through all 52 in/out presets.

name: OriDomi
capabilities: OriDomi slices any element into nested panels (clones of the real DOM) and creases them in 3D, with per-panel shading strips that fake lamp light on each fold. Accordion, curl, ramp, stairs, fracture, twist and fold-up all run on selectable HTML and text, with no canvas or WebGL, and it ships its own touch/drag-to-fold handling.

name: Peel.js
capabilities: Peel.js splits an element into top, back and bottom layers, clips them along a moving fold line with SVG clip paths, and adds shadows and a back-side reflection, so plain HTML peels like a real sticker or page corner. Shapes can be circles, polygons or any SVG path (this sheet has a heart, a starburst and a ticket), and you can tween the peel along a bezier path with setPeelPath and setTimeAlongPath.

name: Swup
capabilities: Swup intercepts links, fetches the next real HTML page and swaps only the container, with CSS classes timing each phase so the transition itself stays plain CSS. This three-page site switches live between the official overlay, slide and fade themes and the parallel plugin, which keeps the old and new pages on screen at the same time.

name: StPageFlip
capabilities: StPageFlip computes the fold line between the grabbed corner and the pointer, then clips, rotates and shades real HTML pages along it, so a turn follows your drag and shows a soft curl or a stiff hardcover swing. This zine is 12 plain HTML pages with container-query typography. It shows the cover alone, opens to spreads on wide screens and drops to single pages on phones.

name: IE Page Transitions
capabilities: It reads the original <meta http-equiv="Page-Enter" content="revealTrans(...)"> tags and plays all 23 effects (blinds, checkerboard, random dissolve, circle out and the rest) through the View Transition API. Pick any effect number in this Win98 Internet Explorer window and move between GeoCities-style pages. Needs a browser that supports View Transition types.

name: Scrollama
capabilities: Scrollama is the small engine behind a lot of Pudding/newsroom-style scrollytelling: it fires step enter/exit events from IntersectionObserver instead of scroll math, and can observe a custom root scroller. Here 96 dots (illustrative data) re-form from a timeline grid into sorted bars, a 24-hour clock and a sunflower disc as each card passes.

name: lax.js
capabilities: lax.js binds any CSS property to a driver value through keyframe arrays, and its drivers can track inertia, a smoothed scroll velocity. That makes speed itself a design input: headlines shear, blur and track out the faster you scroll, while shapes and marquees stay locked to position.

name: Lottie + lottie-interactivity
capabilities: LottieFiles' interactivity layer for lottie-web (5.13.0 here) maps scroll visibility or pointer position straight onto Lottie frames, so a vector After Effects-style timeline becomes a scrubbable scroll scene. Here a self-authored shape-layer animation (trim paths, repeaters, dashed strokes) builds an orbital mark as you scroll, and a second one blooms under your cursor.

name: Zumly
capabilities: Zumly turns any element marked .zoom-me into a portal: click it and the camera scales the current view until the trigger becomes the next view, keeping blurred or dimmed parents in place as spatial context. Views are plain HTML strings, so this dive from a solar system to a planet, a city lens and a lit apartment window is all CSS, with a breadcrumb driven by Zumly's afterZoomIn and afterZoomOut events.

name: Vue Flux
capabilities: Vue Flux slices each slide into DOM tiles, strips or rings and animates them with CSS 3D transforms: book page turns, cube spins, exploding tiles, zips and camera irises, with no canvas or WebGL involved. Here a canvas-painted poster series autoplays through 14 of its transitions, and each chip forces the next slide through that effect.

name: LiquidFun
capabilities: LiquidFun adds a particle solver to Box2D: water, viscous, elastic and rigid particle groups that collide with ordinary rigid bodies. Here about 2,000 particles are splatted into a low-res density field and shaded as a metaball surface with refraction, foam and depth tint, so the water reads as liquid instead of dots. The pink and amber jellies are elastic particle groups pushed around by the same pressure solver.

name: Jolt Physics
capabilities: JoltPhysics.js compiles Jorrit Rouwe's C++ engine to WebAssembly and exposes nearly its full API: layer filters, body interfaces, CCD, sleeping islands. Here a few hundred interlocking bricks stack stably, get smashed by dense continuous-collision cannonballs, then fly back home on a loop. The single-thread .wasm build is about 2 MB and needs no COOP/COEP headers.

name: planck.js
capabilities: A faithful Box2D port that gives you the engine's real joint toolkit: wheel joints with spring suspension and motors, revolute chains, mouse joints, reaction forces you can read every step. Here a motorised car drives an endless procedural course of breakable rope bridges, crate stacks and a Newton's cradle, drawn as a live engineering drawing.

name: cannon-es
capabilities: The pmndrs-maintained ES-module fork of cannon.js: boxes, spheres, contact materials, impulses and sleeping in a tree-shakable package that pairs naturally with three.js. Here 107 box bodies with tuned contact materials carry a real chain reaction through a spiral, then rewind and run again.

name: Party
capabilities: One Engine, swappable force modules: SPH/PIC-FLIP Fluids, boids-style Behavior with chase/avoid by mass, distance Joints with Grab, plus Trails and Lines renderers. It runs WGSL compute on WebGPU and drops to a Canvas2D CPU runtime with the same module API, and any module input can be animated by built-in oscillators (here they rock the tank's gravity).

name: verlet-js
capabilities: verlet-js is the 2013 engine behind the famous canvas spiderweb and cloth demos: everything is particles joined by distance constraints, relaxed a few times per frame. Here an orb web (spokes, a real capture spiral, sagging anchor chains) is built from raw Particles and DistanceConstraints; a spider walks the live constraint graph and its weight dents the silk. Drag uses the engine's own nearestEntity()/draggedEntity, and overstretched or swiped strands are simply removed from the composite.

name: React Spring
capabilities: React Spring animates with real spring physics (tension, friction, mass) instead of durations, so a flung card keeps the velocity your gesture gave it. Paired with @use-gesture, useSprings drives a whole deck from one drag handler, and useTransition/looping springs handle the rest without a single keyframe.

name: Rebound
capabilities: Rebound models springs with the same tension/friction values as Facebook's Origami prototyping tool. That is where the Paper/Pop-era feel came from: anything you can map to 0→1 overshoots and settles like a physical object. One SpringSystem drives every tile here, and a second one on a SteppingSimulationLooper integrates offline to plot the exact step response for the current settings.

name: Dynamics.js
capabilities: Dynamics.js swaps cubic-bezier easing for physical models: spring with anticipation, bounce, gravity and forceWithGravity, each with a few tactile parameters. Every type is a plain function f(t), so one call both plots the curve and drives dynamics.animate. This lab recreates the original dynamicsjs.com editor: live plot with a playhead, onion-skin track and generated code.

name: Smooth Scrollbar
capabilities: smooth-scrollbar replaces native scrolling with its own damped momentum loop, and its official OverscrollPlugin decides what happens after the content runs out: translate the content past the edge (iOS bounce) or paint a curved glow toward the touch point (Android). Here a ghost finger drives the library's real touch and wheel handlers into a phone feed while a live trace plots the overscroll spring.

name: split-flap-elements
capabilities: Each <sfe-cell> is a real mechanical reel: it steps through adjacent values with a top/bottom flap animation instead of cross-fading, and the board coordinates settle order and stagger across cells. Reels can hold whole words, so a remarks column flips between 'BOARDING' and 'DELAYED' like a real Solari board.

name: Hover Tilt
capabilities: Hover Tilt springs an element toward the pointer and paints a moving glare layer, then exposes its live pointer state as CSS variables (--hover-tilt-x, -y, -opacity). That lets plain CSS drive rainbow foil, gold leaf and conic 'cosmos' holo effects inside the card with no extra JavaScript.

name: webaudio-controls
capabilities: g200kg's controls render hardware-style knobs, faders, switches and a playable keyboard as custom elements, styled entirely through a colors attribute or knob sprite strips. They behave like real gear: drag or scroll to turn, and MIDI-learn is built in, so a WebAudio synth panel takes markup rather than a canvas engine.

name: Cuberto Mouse Follower
capabilities: Cuberto's follower replaces the pointer with an eased, velocity-skewed blob that changes state from plain data attributes: data-cursor-text grows it into a label, data-cursor-img turns it into a circular image plate, and data-cursor-stick makes it snap magnetically to buttons. The agency-portfolio cursor without writing hover handlers.

name: Odometer
capabilities: Odometer animates a number change by spinning each digit on its own ribbon, so 128,406 to 128,506 rolls like a mechanical counter instead of swapping text. Its themes (car, slot machine, train station, digital) are plain CSS, and update() is all the API you need.

name: p5.brush
capabilities: p5.brush simulates real media: pencils and pens with pressure and texture, vector-field-bent strokes, hatching, and watercolor fills that bleed, pool and granulate at their edges. Its standalone build runs on a plain canvas, so generative art gets a hand-made quality without shaders of your own.

name: segment-display
capabilities: <segment-display> draws beveled seven- or sixteen-segment LED glyphs on a canvas, with unlit segments still faintly visible, and scrolls text longer than the display like a marquee. Fill colors, segment width, bevel and spacing are all properties, so one element can pass for an amber VFD or a red clock.

name: Boring Avatars
capabilities: Boring Avatars hashes a name into one of six geometric SVG styles (beam, marble, pixel, sunset, ring, bauhaus) drawn from your five-color palette. Output is deterministic inline SVG, so a user list gets a consistent, on-brand look instead of grey silhouettes.

name: Dice Box
capabilities: Dice Box runs BabylonJS rendering and AmmoJS physics in web workers on an OffscreenCanvas, so real d4–d100 meshes tumble, collide and settle while the main thread stays free. The canvas is transparent and the dice cast shadows, so you can set them on any tabletop you style in CSS, and onRollComplete returns per-die values you can show in your own UI.

name: Fracture
capabilities: Fracture captures a real element to a texture, hides it, and replaces it with extruded 3D shards on a WebGL overlay. Its crack algorithm radiates and branches cracks from the impact point, so you get fine splinters near the hit and large plates farther out, which reads more like glass than Voronoi cells do. Pieces drift in slow motion with depth-of-field blur, and you can strike them again in mid-air. Here a bento grid of cards shatters wherever you tap and rebuilds itself when left idle.

name: RageLayer
capabilities: RageLayer rasterizes the real DOM into a destructible canvas, so bullets punch actual holes through your text, fire chars it away and a chainsaw loop drops the cut-out out of the page as one rigid body. Fifteen procedural tools (no model or audio assets), a rigid-body debris solver, undo checkpoints and a headless ToolbarModel let you drive it from your own UI. Here a broadsheet gets wrecked by an idle demo reel fired through engine.strike(), then swept back.

name: SnapDOM
capabilities: SnapDOM clones a live element into an SVG foreignObject and rasterizes it in milliseconds. Web fonts, pseudo-elements, gradients, clip-paths and mid-animation states come through intact. Here every shutter press freezes the animated CSS postcard into a canvas that develops on a corkboard, and the capture time is shown so you can check the speed claim yourself.

name: vault66-crt-effect
capabilities: A <crt-effect> web component that layers scanlines, a sweep bar, edge glow, flicker, curved-glass shading, static and chromatic glitch over whatever you slot inside it, with no canvas or WebGL involved. The text underneath stays real DOM: selectable, focusable, typeable. Every look is an attribute, so presets and overrides swap at runtime with setAttribute.

name: crt-shader
capabilities: Instead of overlaying scanline stripes, crt-shader rebuilds the picture in three GPU passes: horizontal signal spread, brightness-dependent beam width, then phosphor mask and optics. Bright pixels get fatter scanlines and dark ones thin out, as on a real tube. The core renderer has no dependencies and accepts any canvas, so a live procedural pixel scene can be fed through it every frame.

name: QR Code Styling
capabilities: Instead of black squares, qr-code-styling draws every module as a shape — dots, classy teardrops, extra-rounded blobs — with separate styles for the corner finder squares and their centers, linear or radial gradients, a circle shape and a knocked-out center logo, all as SVG or canvas. This designer exposes the real options live: swipe the chips, rotate the gradient, and export the exact SVG.

name: <qr-code> (bitjson)
capabilities: <qr-code> renders each module, finder ring and center icon as separate SVG nodes, so animateQRCode() can stagger them by grid position: ripple out from the center, materialize at random, or fly in from your own keyframe function. This demo runs the five built-in presets plus three custom ones (Scatter, Vortex, Rain) written against the same (targets, x, y, count, entity) API.

name: Awesome-qr.js
capabilities: Awesome-qr.js draws every QR module as a scaled dot and re-composites the code onto each frame of a GIF background, returning a new animated GIF as a data URL. Finder and timing patterns stay solid while the data dots let the artwork show through, so the code stays scannable. Here the GIF loops are generated in the browser with gifenc and handed to Awesome-qr as gifBackground.

name: useAnimations
capabilities: Each useAnimations icon ships with its own behaviour: menus and hearts toggle on click, the trash can opens on hover, loaders loop, and a built-in 8 kB player renders the Lottie data as SVG with no lottie-web dependency. Icons follow currentColor, so a theme swatch recolours the whole console, and toggles are controlled through the active prop.

name: Material Line Icons (line-md)
capabilities: Vjacheslav Trushkin's line-md set animates each icon's strokes with SMIL inside the SVG itself, so icons draw in with no JavaScript runtime, and dedicated transition icons morph menu into close, play into pause and moon into sun. The demo renders icons from the Iconify JSON package with @iconify/utils; inserting a fresh SVG replays its draw-on.

name: DiceBear
capabilities: DiceBear turns a seed string into the same avatar every time, in any of its style definitions, from Notionists and Open Peeps to pixel art, glass and identicons. Version 10 splits the renderer (@dicebear/core) from JSON style definitions (@dicebear/styles), and each style carries its own license in its meta block. This demo loads only the CC0 and MIT styles and checks that license at runtime.

name: Blobatar
capabilities: Blobatar turns any name into a geometric creature with two capsule eyes, and its optional motion layer adds idle breathing, blinking and pointer-tracking gaze. Expressions such as happy, wink or thinking are imported as values and morph from the current pose. Here every face aims its gaze at a wandering firefly until the mouse moves.

name: dither-avatar
capabilities: dither-avatar hashes a seed into a hue pair and a gradient angle, then orders it through a 4×4 Bayer matrix on a 34×34 grid and writes the result as one SVG path. The output is a few hundred bytes of crisp, scalable 1-bit art with no dependencies. The roster renders each member from their handle.

name: bwip-js
capabilities: bwip-js is a JavaScript port of Barcode Writer in Pure PostScript, so it covers symbologies most generators skip: MaxiCode's hexagonal bullseye, DotCode, Han Xin, Code One, stacked Code 16K and the 4-state postal codes. toSVG returns clean vector markup for any of them. The demo encodes one string in twelve formats.

name: ipad-cursor
capabilities: Replaces the system cursor with a soft disc that snaps onto data-cursor="block" elements, takes their exact size and corner radius, and pulls them magnetically toward the pointer; over data-cursor="text" it thins into a caret sized to the type. Here a ghost pointer tours a glass notes app until you take over (touch drags drive it too).

name: perfect-cursors
capabilities: Steve Ruiz's tiny library behind tldraw's live cursors: feed it the positions your socket delivers at 4-15 Hz and it animates a smooth spline through them at display rate. The left board teleports to each packet; the right board renders the same packets through PerfectCursor, with its interpolated trail drawn behind each collaborator.

name: img-comparison-slider
capabilities: A single <img-comparison-slider> element with first/second slots, a slot="handle" for your own knob, and CSS variables for the divider and default handle. Slots take any element, so here the 'after' pane is a canvas that re-dithers the photo (Atkinson, Bayer, Game Boy, RGB halftone) at runtime; keyboard arrows, touch drag, hover-follow and a vertical direction for portrait come with the element.

name: party.js
capabilities: party.js renders particles as real DOM elements with 3D CSS transforms, so any SVG or div can become a particle and is lit by a brightness filter as it tumbles. Register your own shapes in party.resolvableShapes, drive size/opacity/rotation over lifetime with ModuleBuilder splines, or build a full emitter; bursts can originate from an element, a Rect/Circle or the pointer event itself.

name: Devices.css
capabilities: Every bezel, Dynamic Island, button and hinge is plain CSS: gradients, box-shadows and pseudo-elements, with no images or SVG. Because .device-screen is an ordinary element, you can put a real responsive UI inside it. Here one live flight tracker runs on a MacBook Pro, iPad Pro, iPhone 14 Pro and Watch Ultra, and finish classes like device-gold swap the hardware colour.

name: react-3d-mockups
capabilities: The iPhone is generated from code at runtime: CSG cuts the ports and camera plateau, and no GLB files are loaded. The screen is real DOM placed on the glass with CSS 3D transforms and masked by the depth buffer, so a React component keeps rendering while you orbit the phone. Retail colorways and variants are plain props, and the canvas only redraws when something moves.

name: Atrament
capabilities: Atrament smooths every stroke and modulates its width by drawing speed or stylus pressure, so lines taper like a real pen instead of plotting at a fixed width. Here its programmatic beginStroke/draw/endStroke API brushes an ensō and a plum branch, its worker-based flood fill colours the blossoms and wash hills, and erase mode carves the seal. Then the brush is yours.

name: drauu
capabilities: drauu turns any <svg> into a drawing surface: a pressure-aware perfect-freehand stylus, lines with arrowheads, dashed rectangles, ellipses, a line eraser and undo/redo, all saved as plain SVG elements you can style or dump(). Here synthetic pen events go through drauu's own pointer listeners, so a virtual presenter marks up a QBR slide and then hands you the pen.

name: cards-css
capabilities: One createHoloCard() call gives you spring-physics tilt, glare and any of 14 foils (prism, oilslick, mosaic, sunburst, gold...), several built from seeded, code-generated textures instead of image files. Here each card face is drawn to a canvas from original art, and the hero card is driven by synthetic pointer events, so the foil keeps moving even when nobody touches it.

name: MetalUI
capabilities: MetalUI components look like moulded objects rather than flat UI: bone or graphite plastic, sunk wells, latching keys with lamps, a knurled slider knob and dot-matrix displays that step six times a second without tweening. The console here drives the Weather slab's sky, sun and moon live, and the colourway switch swaps the whole device between bone and graphite.

name: RPGUI
capabilities: Add rpgui-* classes to plain HTML and you get gilded pixel frames, parchment buttons, segmented HP/MP bars, golden sliders, dropdowns and inventory icons, all drawn from the library's own pixel art. The sheet is playable: drink potions, rest, train toward a level-up, and scrub the time of day to repaint the pixel landscape behind the panels.

name: Sakura.js
capabilities: Each petal is a plain div with a random gradient and border-radius, sent down by three stacked CSS animations (fall, blow, sway) so the drift looks wind-driven with no canvas. Swap the colour list and petal class and the same engine does maple leaves, ginkgo or snow; tapping the scene spawns a short, dense second instance as a gust.

name: LDRS
capabilities: LDRS ships 44 loaders (quantum, helix, newton's cradle, squircle...) as tiny custom elements that take size, color, speed and stroke attributes, with React wrappers too. The wall registers every one of them; tap any tile to inspect it big with its live markup, retime the whole set with one speed multiplier, or recolour it.

name: SVG Spinners
capabilities: n3r4zzurr0's spinners animate with SMIL inside the SVG itself, so they move as an , inline SVG or CSS mask with no JavaScript, and every fill is currentColor. Here they sit in the places spinners actually live (a deploy button, a search field, a CI pipeline, a typing bubble) and any of the 46 can be dropped into any slot.

name: Whirl
capabilities: Whirl is 90 hand-made CSS loaders (a book flipping pages, Pac-Man, pong, a rainbow behind clouds) that each need only a class and a few empty divs, coloured through --primary and --secondary. The board deals them onto bold flat tiles, promotes one to a hero tile with its markup, and keeps re-dealing while idle.

name: Flip
capabilities: Flip renders each digit as a real two-panel card that folds on a 3D hinge with moving shadow and highlight, and a declarative transform chain (preset(d,h,m,s) -> pad -> split -> delay) turns any value into staggered flips. Here one countdown and two live counters share a reskinned Bebas Neue card with a measured optical-centre fix and a Graphite/Ivory finish toggle.

name: canvas-gauges
capabilities: Every part of the dial is an option: plate gradients, tick sets, redline highlights, needle shape and shadow, value box and per-element fonts. This cluster restyles four RadialGauges into an amber night dash with a bundled Oswald face, and a small drive simulation pushes speed, revs, fuel and coolant into them every frame.

name: Precision Inputs
capabilities: Precision Inputs turns a hidden range input into an FL Studio-style SVG dial: drag, wheel, double-click reset and keyboard all come free, and FLReactiveGripDial morphs grip bumps into the knob while you hold it. Here four dials drive a procedural viewfinder where aperture sets bokeh size and blade shape, focus racks between rain-on-glass, a neon sign and the city, and shutter stretches the rain into streaks.

name: Ambient CSS
capabilities: Ambient CSS derives every box-shadow, chamfer highlight, groove and surface tint from a few custom properties (--amb-light-x/y, key and fill intensity) with coefficients fitted to Blender renders. Move the light and the whole hardware UI relights coherently; drop the key light and the lume markings start to glow. @ambientcss/components layers React knobs, faders, switches and key banks on top.

name: goey-toast
capabilities: Each toast is an SVG blob, not a box. A loading pill oozes out, then the same shape bulges into a full card with a description and action button when the promise settles, and collapses back to a pill before it leaves. Spring bounce, fill and border colour are all props, and it uses the Sonner API you already know.

name: Sileo
capabilities: Sileo draws each toast as a gooey SVG shape that springs from a compact pill into a card and back. Toasts that share an id shape-shift in place, so one island can morph from AirPods to upload spinner to a photo summary. Only the newest toast expands while older ones stay as pills, which gives you the Dynamic Island feel without any extra config.

name: ScratchCard-js
capabilities: ScratchCard-js puts a canvas 'foil' over any HTML or image and erases it with a line, spray, circle or custom brush. It reports the scratched percentage and fires a callback once you pass a threshold. Here each of nine cells is its own card, with procedurally drawn foil and SVG prize symbols under a spray brush.

name: Spin Wheel
capabilities: spin-wheel is a dependency-free canvas wheel: items carry their own weight and colours, labels auto-size to fit, and a rotating image plus a fixed overlay image let you dress it any way you like. spinToItem() lands on a chosen slice with your own easing, and onRest/onCurrentIndexChange drive the result card and the pointer's tick animation. This demo switches between three generated themes (carnival marquee, neon arcade, bistro), each with its own font.

name: React Bits
capabilities: React Bits ships its effects as editable source files through the shadcn CLI, each in JS/TS and CSS/Tailwind variants. Dither is a dependency-free WebGL2 shader: ordered Bayer, halftone, line and crosshatch screens over a flowing noise field, with cursor ripples and custom palettes.

The text side of React Bits: GSAP-driven SplitText, a pointer-aware ShinyText sweep, DecryptedText that scrambles glyphs under the cursor, Magnet buttons with tilt, and ClickSpark bursts on a canvas layer. Each is one file you own and tune via props.

Ten full-bleed shader backgrounds (Silk, Galaxy, Iridescence, Balatro, LiquidEther, Aurora, Orb, LiquidChrome, Lightning, Threads) each dropped behind the same landing-page hero as a single component, with type and accent re-tuned per background. Every one is a raw-WebGL TSX file with art-direction props (sheen, warp, pixelSize, crt, clickSwirl…) and built-in pointer reactions, so a hero background is one line of JSX and no video or image assets.

React Bits' text set treats type as a live material: TextPressure and VariableProximity drive Roboto Flex's weight, width and optical-size axes from the pointer, ASCIIText re-renders a word as a tilting WebGL glyph field, and SplitFlapText builds a mechanical departures board out of CSS flaps. This demo composes ten of them into five scenes — poster, specimen sheet, ASCII 3D, departures board and a fuzzy/glitch 404 — each moving on its own at idle and following touch drags.

React Bits' cursor set ranges from a WebGL stable-fluids solver and a three.js chrome metaball to spring-chained ribbons, a GSAP poster trail and SDF contour metaballs. Each one is a single file in your repo that you can edit, and each exposes detailed physics and material props (goo, swirl, decay, lock-on). This demo puts eight of them on their own scenes behind a switcher, with an idle autopilot path and touch-drag support.

Nine card components composed into four switchable layouts: a spotlight bento with particles and magnetic tilt, a grayscale ChromaGrid that recolours under a cursor-following mask and drives a holographic ProfileCard, two physics card decks, and a WebGL ElectricBorder around a pixel-dissolve card next to a draggable Folder. Each one is a single TSX file you own and restyle with props.

Four of React Bits' gallery components share one 14-image set: a bent WebGL ring with wave distortion, an infinite drag-to-spin sphere, a CSS-3D dome you look around inside, and a spring-physics masonry wall with drag-to-reorder and a lightbox. The WebGL and CSS galleries take the same plain image array, so switching layouts is a single prop change.

A fake desktop OS built from four React Bits pieces: a spring-physics magnifying Dock with badges, hop-on-click and long-press menus; GooeyNav tabs whose pill and particles merge in a WebGL metaball pass; a FlowingMenu whose marquee band follows the cursor between rows; and ElasticSliders that rubber-band past their ends. The sliders drive the wallpaper's brightness and warmth live.

Lanyard is a pure three.js rope-and-rigid-body simulation: the strap is a jointed band with twist, the card has real inertia, and a holographic-foil shader adds diffraction rainbows and glints that track the light as it swings. Here the badge front, back and strap are painted on a 2D canvas at runtime and passed in as images, with LogoLoop running the library marquee underneath.

A 1986-style boot screen with five swappable phosphor 'screens' (FaultyTerminal, LetterGlitch, PixelBlast, CRTWarp, GradientASCII) under a Noise grain/scanline overlay and a typed VT323 boot log with a working prompt. Each screen is a single WebGL component with its own CRT click effect (degauss, tear, ripple, retune, burst), so the retro look comes from props rather than hand-written shaders.

name: Magic UI
capabilities: Magic UI is a free shadcn registry of 150+ motion components aimed at marketing pages. AnimatedBeam draws gradient SVG paths between any two refs and recomputes them on resize; BorderBeam, NumberTicker and FlickeringGrid add the light-trail, spring-counter and canvas-noise layers.

name: Aceternity UI
capabilities: Aceternity UI collects theatrical effects for hero sections: cards with real CSS 3D depth, SVG beam backgrounds, spotlights, word-by-word blur reveals. In CardContainer each CardItem gets its own translateZ, so layers separate in perspective as the cursor tilts the card.

name: Animate UI
capabilities: Animate UI is a shadcn-style distribution where every primitive animates: backgrounds, text, buttons, Radix wrappers. Here the gooey BubbleBackground follows the cursor while SlidingNumber rolls each digit of a live clock, RotatingText cycles words and HighlightText sweeps a marker.

name: Motion Primitives
capabilities: Motion Primitives packages Motion layout animations into drop-in parts. MorphingDialog shares layout IDs between a card and its dialog, so the image, title and container travel as one shape instead of cross-fading. TextEffect, TextShimmer, BorderTrail and InfiniteSlider cover the text and ambient motion.

name: Sonner
capabilities: Sonner's stack is the reference toast design: notifications pile up as cards with depth, fan out on hover and dismiss on swipe. One <Toaster /> and a global toast() function cover success, error, promise lifecycles, actions and rich colours, with no provider or context setup.

name: Vaul
capabilities: Vaul brings the iOS sheet to the web: drag or flick to dismiss with velocity-aware physics, and shouldScaleBackground shrinks the page behind it into a rounded card. It is built on Radix Dialog, so focus trapping and accessibility come built in, and it ships no styles of its own.

name: cmdk
capabilities: cmdk is the headless engine under shadcn/ui's Command and many ⌘K menus. It handles filtering, ranking, keyboard navigation and grouping, and exposes plain data attributes for styling. Nested pages are just conditional children.

name: 8bitcn
capabilities: Every shadcn primitive redrawn with stepped pixel borders and Press Start 2P type, plus game-specific blocks: health, mana and XP bars, enemy displays, dialogue boxes, quest logs. You get a whole retro RPG HUD from a registry instead of a sprite sheet.

name: Ephemera
capabilities: Ephemera renders interface pieces as real stationery: an envelope you open, a ticket stub you tear off, a receipt that prints, rubber stamps, a polaroid that develops. Six paper stocks (cream, kraft, ledger, blueprint, newsprint, carbon) are swapped with a single data-paper attribute.

name: Kokonut UI
capabilities: Kokonut leans into physical metaphors: a lamp with a pull cord that toggles dark mode, a detent dial that clicks between values, a liquid-fill slider and slide-to-confirm. Each control borrows the feel of a real object instead of being another flat toggle.

name: audiocn
capabilities: audiocn is a pro-audio control kit: LED level meters with real ballistics, a console fader with dB taper, aluminium-cap knobs, an LCD readout, spectrum and a lightning-styled waveform. Components subscribe to a frame source and paint outside React, so meters stay smooth at 60fps.

name: neobrutalism.dev
capabilities: neobrutalism.dev restyles the shadcn component set with 2px black borders, solid offset shadows that collapse when pressed, and one loud main colour driven by CSS variables. Swap --main or --shadow and the whole dashboard, including Recharts charts, follows.

name: soundcn
capabilities: soundcn ships each sound as a registry item: a tiny TypeScript module with the audio inlined as a data URI, plus a useSound hook on top of Web Audio. Clicks, chimes and buzzes are copied into your repo, with no CDN fetch or audio library.

name: Fancy Components
capabilities: Fancy's Gravity wraps any DOM element in a Matter.js body, so real styled HTML pills tumble, stack and can be thrown, while staying selectable and themeable with Tailwind. It's for the kind of interactive editorial hero you'd normally build from scratch.

Typography components that animate OpenType variation axes directly: weight, width and slant swell around the cursor, letters breathe, and a ribbon of text rides an SVG path. It shows what variable fonts can do beyond picking a static weight.

name: lucide-animated
capabilities: Each Lucide icon gets its own motion choreography (bells ring, rockets lift off, cogs spin) and installs as one file. An imperative startAnimation() handle lets you drive them from code, like the diagonal waves rippling across this grid.

name: Motion Core
capabilities: Motion Core ships WebGL image components you copy into a Svelte 5 project with its CLI. One portrait runs through three of them: AsciiRenderer turns it into scanline-glitched phosphor glyphs, DitheredImage applies Bayer, halftone or void-and-cluster ordered dithering, and WatercolorImage paints it with an anisotropic brush filter. A wipe compares each against the source.

Motion Core's background shaders are ordinary Svelte components whose props feed shader uniforms. Here LiquidMetal, GlitterCloth, GodRays and PlasmaGrid fill the frame, and the pointer drives their props live (wave frequency, light-source position, hue). The prop values you are steering show up as JSX-style markup under the title.
installs: npx @motion-core/cli add liquid-metal glitter-cloth god-rays plasma-grid

name: CrafterUI
capabilities: CrafterUI's mercury set (mercury-dial, mercury-menu, built on mercury-surface) renders menus as one SVG metaball: drops ooze out of the button, overshoot on a spring and dive back in with a splat, and any drop can be grabbed and pulled into a liquid finger. It's calibrated so the gooey rim matches a crisp 1px CSS border at every blur level, and it themes through ordinary shadcn tokens. Here those tokens pour it in chrome.

name: threecn
capabilities: threecn ships 28 copy-in R3F scenes that color themselves from your shadcn CSS variables (--primary, --accent), so re-theming a 3D scene is just setting tokens. This switcher cycles five of them — Aizawa attractor, a 4D tesseract, a boids flock, a pendulum wave and a golden-angle bloom — re-skinning each by rewriting :root variables, with one WebGL canvas alive at a time.

The effects side of threecn: a hyperspace warp tunnel, a Voronoi-fractured sphere that breathes apart, curl-noise particle filaments and additive aurora ribbons. Every scene is plain R3F source you own after install, and each one recolors live from shadcn theme tokens.

name: NS UI
capabilities: NS UI's ASCII backgrounds are real simulations, not noise textures: an Ising lattice inks only its domain walls, a Gray-Scott solver inks only the ridge of its reaction fronts, a q-model packing inks only load-bearing force chains. Each one treats the pointer as part of the physics: a lens, a magnetic field, a pipette, a throttle. This gallery cycles through eight of them.

These are working form controls built on physical mechanisms. The slider tunes a Chladni plate until the sand locks onto its nodal lines, the numeric input reads like a vernier caliper, the stepper clicks through a ratchet and pawl, and the button heat-soaks when you press it too often. Each one is a normal controlled React input with value and onValueChange.

name: Componentry
capabilities: Componentry is a shadcn-installable set of creative components that leans hard on retro raster looks: a canvas ASCII renderer with flow and glitch modes, a Floyd–Steinberg particle logo, and a dithered prism shader hero. Each one lands as a single readable .tsx file you own, with few or no dependencies beyond React.

Four Componentry toys share one cursor: particle type that scatters, eyes that follow and blink, a magnet-line field, and a split-flap departure board. When nobody is touching it, a ghost cursor drives them all. Each toy is a self-contained shadcn registry file, so you can drop in one without adopting a framework.

name: Crucible
capabilities: Crucible ships each background as one self-contained component: OGL fragment shaders (Corona's aurora curtains, Cathode's CRT tracking tear, Plasma, Umbra, Warp, Ember) and 2D-canvas sims (Cinder, the seeded Arc lightning) that share a harness with DPR caps, pausing when offscreen, and reduced-motion still frames. The text effects follow the same forge theme: Cipher scrambles through rune glyphs before it settles, Gild sweeps a champagne highlight across the letters, and Fracture splits the text into sheared channel ghosts.

Three of Crucible's field components side by side. Filings is a single-draw-call shader whose iron-filing segments bend toward the cursor, Fireflies is an additive-glow canvas swarm, and Flurry snaps its snowfall to a hard pixel grid with depth layers and gusts. Their speed, drift and wind props update live with no rebuild, so each panel here maps them directly to the pointer.

name: Atelier UI
capabilities: Atelier UI is a shadcn registry of WebGL effects that all render through a single shared canvas (WebglProvider + WebglScene), so a sphere, orbit rings and a spiral stair each get their own camera without spawning extra GL contexts. This demo swaps between its Sphere, Orbit and Spiral galleries through the kit's pixel- and band-cover page transitions, with TextScramble titles.

name: Hyperiux Vault
capabilities: Hyperiux Vault hands you the full source of studio-style effects instead of a package: Fractal Glass refracts any image through ribbed glass strips in a three.js shader, and Milky Way runs an 80k-particle GPGPU galaxy with smoke flow and edge-blur post-processing in react-three-fiber. The free tier (56 effects) is MPL-2.0, so you own and can tweak every shader.
installs: npx hyperiux@latest login && npx hyperiux@latest add fractal-glass

name: AnimateIcons
capabilities: Every icon has its own Motion choreography (bells swing, rockets lift off, trash lids flip) and exposes startAnimation()/stopAnimation() through a ref, so you can trigger it from anywhere, not only on hover. This wall fires those handles as a distance-timed ripple from whatever you tap, across both style sets, with live speed and colour props.

name: Canvas UI
capabilities: Canvas UI components wrap ordinary HTML and run it through a WebGL shader, using Chrome's experimental HTML-in-Canvas API (drawElementImage) so the content stays clickable while it is being rendered as pixels. Here <Asciify> turns a space-weather dashboard into colored 5x5 glyphs inside a drifting lens; the tabs and buttons underneath still work. Browsers without the API get the library's own DOM-snapshot fallback; the badge shows which path is running.

Each Canvas UI effect takes a live HTML subtree, captures it with Chrome's HTML-in-Canvas API and re-renders it as a liquid sim, glass shards, a page curl, water ripples, wind-blown cloth or VHS tape, while the seat buttons and check-in button keep working. Without the API, only the overlay-style shaders (Liquid, Ripple, VHS) are offered, and a badge names the chrome://flags switch that turns on the rest.
installs: npx shadcn@latest add https://canvasui.dev/r/liquid-react.json https://canvasui.dev/r/shatter-react.json https://canvasui.dev/r/peel-react.json https://canvasui.dev/r/ripple-react.json https://canvasui.dev/r/cloth-react.json https://canvasui.dev/r/vhs-react.json

name: 1st-pouf
capabilities: 1st-pouf builds every control from a three-shadow clay recipe (top highlight, inner floor lip, soft drop), so buttons, sliders and toggles read as soft cushions that press in when engaged. The recipe and palette are plain CSS tokens: here the Puff slider rewrites the shadow depth live and the colour switch swaps the accent token across every component at once.

name: Uiverse Galaxy
capabilities: Uiverse's open-source Galaxy repo holds 3,000+ single-file HTML+CSS elements by hundreds of authors: no JS, no framework, paste and go. This wall mounts 15 of the odder ones (a haunted-house loader, a hamster wheel, a sprouting toggle, an isometric Enter keycap, eyes that follow the cursor) unmodified, each in its own shadow root so the authors' class names never collide.
installs: git clone https://github.com/uiverse-io/galaxy (or copy-paste any element's HTML+CSS from uiverse.io)

name: Benday
capabilities: Benday rasterizes a logo once into a grid of comic-print dots (coverage, tone and depth from a distance transform), then animates every dot through one of 21 presets. The loading indicator becomes the brand mark itself, and it springs into a crisp logo when state flips to done. It is a shadcn registry component that renders to a single canvas with no dependencies.

name: agentfaces
capabilities: One <AgentFace> component maps agent work states (listening, thinking, working, needs-you, speaking, done) to blinks, gaze drift, springy body motion and glyph morphs: the body turns into a check mark on done and a heart when held smitten. Here a scripted chat drives the face through a full agent loop, with a simulated voice moving the mouth while it streams.

name: Meteocons
capabilities: Each Meteocon carries its animation inside the SVG file as SMIL: rain falls, bolts flash, fog drifts, the Beaufort windsock spins. That means a plain animates with zero JavaScript or runtime. The forecast here swaps between the fill, flat, line and monochrome sets and day/night variants of the same conditions.

name: Animotion
capabilities: Animotion turns a Reveal.js deck into Svelte components: every fragment step is an <Action> that runs code, so slides can tween SVG state and morph code with Shiki Magic Move instead of swapping static bullets. This deck auto-plays a code block that rewrites itself while the circle it describes actually moves, then a bubble sort whose bar positions are tweens.

name: UI Capsule
capabilities: UI Capsule ships oddball interaction pieces as copy-in shadcn blocks. chibi-plants is a raymarched SDF character on an XPBD soft-body rig: grab and stretch it, toss it, and its eyes follow your cursor, with variants morphing as one continuous surface.

Three UI Capsule blocks rebuild phone-OS moments with Motion springs inside matte clay phone shells: an AirDrop ripple radar, iOS jiggle-mode home screen with drag-to-reorder, and an Android 9-dot pattern lock. These are real pointer gestures, not videos.

name: 000h (cojeev-ui)
capabilities: One sculpture geometry, five materials: a three.js glass shader that refracts a procedural studio, a spring-back particle cloud, and canvas prints in engraved crosshatch, error-diffusion dither and ASCII glyphs. Studio colours are read from CSS variables, so the glass re-lights when you change the theme. Ships with its own warm paper tokens, DM Sans and Bricolage Grotesque.

name: Isometric
capabilities: Each figure is a hand-built isometric scene drawn as plain SVG paths: towers rise on springs near the pointer, reactor coils charge, a cube twists by layer. It inherits shadcn tokens, so recoloring it to a blueprint is five CSS variables, and every figure reports a live caption through onRead.

The same registry ships a buildable isometric town (World) whose church, reactor and pulley are the line figures as live entities, plus block-game UI: Hotbar, Inventory, HeartsMeter and XpBar. It's all SVG and shadcn tokens, so the night mode here is the world swapping to a .dark token set.

name: Evil Buttons
capabilities: A copy-in shadcn registry of mischievous buttons: one dodges the cursor until its stamina runs out, one makes you drag a handle across a fuse, one guilt-trips you through escalating prompts, one raises horns and canvas fire while held. Each is a single dependency-light TSX file (motion, WebGL or Matter.js where needed) with careful dark-surface shading, so the joke ships with production-grade polish.

name: AI Canvas
capabilities: AI Canvas components are self-contained little objects rather than primitives: a swipeable flip calendar, a dot-matrix neon clock, a halo of 3D-orbiting type, a theme switch you pull like a window blind, and caution tape that shudders when touched. Each is one framer-motion TSX file with its own palette and dark/light handling.

AI Canvas's background set is plain canvas-2D React components that bend toward the pointer: a constellation web that pinches toward the cursor, a lattice that sparks at its intersections, a scan-line sphere that twists, magnetic dots, a warping grid, and a flow field. No WebGL and no dependencies beyond React. A ghost cursor drives them until you take over.

name: Pixelium Design
capabilities: Every border, shadow and corner is rasterized onto canvas as stair-stepped pixels, so buttons, sliders, tabs and dialogs look like an SNES menu rather than a font swap. One call (setPixelSize) re-renders the whole UI at a chunkier grid, setThemeColor builds an OKlab palette from a single hex, and dark/light is a built-in hook. Ships its own Fusion Pixel font (OFL).

name: Soonish
capabilities: Every Soonish loader is the same 25 lamps driven by one CSS keyframe per dot — procedural delay maps plus pre-compiled linear() brightness fields — so there is no JS animation loop and no canvas. Installed as source through the shadcn CLI, each loader is a typed <Loader name> with size, dotSize, speed and color props.

name: loading.dev
capabilities: Each indicator is a small SVG/DOM component whose motion lives in deduplicated <style precedence> CSS and is tuned through custom properties (--ld-size, --ld-duration, --ld-play-state). Shared props like easing="stacked" (two composited rotations) and cap give the set a consistent, detailed feel, and reduced motion is respected out of the box.

name: Bevel
capabilities: Bevel ships 120+ Base UI + Tailwind v4 components that copy real hardware down to its behaviour: the engine telegraph shows your order and the engine room's answer as two pointers, motorized faders drive themselves when someone else moves them, and the guarded switch needs its cover lifted before it will flip. Light, depth and materials come from shared CSS tokens, so brass, bakelite and anodized themes restyle the whole panel.

name: TheGridCN
capabilities: A shadcn registry of 144 Tron-styled items: grid floors, CRT scanlines, circuit backdrops, radar, gauges, HUD corner frames. Colour comes from swappable god theme items (Ares red, Tron cyan, Athena gold, Poseidon blue…), and a data-tron-intensity attribute dials every component's neon glow from flat to full HUD.

name: Tactile UI
capabilities: Each piece is physically simulated rather than animated: the odometer's drums only turn while the one to their right carries, the compass card swings through damping liquid past its mark, and the pull-cord is a spring chain with a detent that snaps. Everything is lit from one fixed room lamp, and a single data-finish attribute re-machines the whole bench from aluminium to graphite.

name: Cult UI
capabilities: Cult UI is a copy-in shadcn registry whose components lean on physical materials instead of flat chrome: nested hairline borders for texture cards, a WebGL liquid-metal ring (metal-fx) around buttons, an SVG feTurbulence/feDisplacementMap glass pane, and inset-shadow neumorph keys. Each item installs as plain Tailwind + React source you own and can retheme.

name: Liveline
capabilities: Benji Taylor's Liveline streams points into a single canvas and lerps everything: the value, the Y-axis range, the badge color. The live head pulses and throws momentum chevrons, candles morph into a line and back, and 'degen' mode bursts particles and shakes the chart on big swings.

name: ThreeUI Community
capabilities: ThreeUI ships art-directed WebGL scenes as drop-in React components, not primitives: TempleNightScene builds a whole Kage mountain temple (terrain, pagoda, torii, lanterns, foliage, fog, bloom) from code with zero textures loaded. Quality, bloom and shadow are live controls, and the camera follows the pointer.

Nine of ThreeUI's WebGL/canvas backgrounds (stream ribbons, an energy orb, a typography vortex, bell-field caustics, dotted ribbon terrain and more), each code-split and swapped live behind the page. Below them is a dock of the kit's art-directed CTA buttons: thermal glow, a 3D keycap, Lumen and an embossed circle.

name: uselayouts
capabilities: A shadcn registry of 60+ React + Motion components, each built around a physical metaphor: a notebook whose pages riffle open in CSS 3D, Polaroids that fan from one corner, a charcoal sleeve that pulls a letter out and flips it toward you. You copy the source into your app, so every spring and shadow stays editable.

name: p5.js
capabilities: p5.js keeps Processing's setup()/draw() mental model: immediate-mode drawing, built-in Perlin noise and an event loop you never have to wire up. Thousands of particles riding a noise field with additive trails take about sixty lines in instance mode, so it slots into any bundle without globals.

name: Elementary Audio
capabilities: Elementary treats sound like React treats UI: you return a tree of el.* nodes and the wasm engine reconciles it against what is already playing, so edits re-render without clicks or restarts. Here the same patch drives a realtime AudioWorklet and an offline renderer that paints the L/R XY scope before you ever press play.

name: Tone.js
capabilities: Tone.js wraps raw Web Audio in musician vocabulary: '16n' note values, a sample-accurate Transport, PolySynths, reverbs and feedback delays you chain like pedals. Tone.getDraw() syncs DOM updates to scheduled audio time, which is why the playhead never drifts from the beat.

name: xterm.js
capabilities: xterm.js is a full VT emulator: true-color ANSI, cursor addressing, the alternate screen buffer and correct Unicode widths, fast enough for full-screen TUIs. Pipe it to a WebSocket for a real shell, or, as here, a fifty-line fake shell running neofetch, matrix rain and a spinning ASCII donut.

name: Kaplay
capabilities: Kaplay (the community continuation of Kaboom.js) builds game objects from component lists like sprite(), area(), body() and doubleJump(), so physics, collisions and tweens are one call each. Every sprite here is pixel art generated from strings into a canvas, and an autopilot plays until you take over.

name: Paper.js
capabilities: Paper.js gives canvas a retained vector model: paths with Bézier segments, smoothing, hit-testing and robust boolean operations like unite, subtract and exclude. Here breathing blobs are united and cut by a cursor blob every frame, with the resulting segments and handles drawn the way an illustration tool would show them.

name: Pts
capabilities: Pts reduces everything to points and groups of points, with geometry helpers (Delaunay, Voronoi, polygon centroids, Num utilities) and a Space/Form split that separates the math from how it's drawn. A drifting point set becomes lit stained glass in a few dozen lines, and the pointer is just one more site.

name: Mafs
capabilities: Mafs turns math diagrams into JSX: coordinates, parametric plots, vectors and draggable points that snap and constrain, with Computer Modern type for an authentic textbook feel. This Bézier construction recomputes every interpolation level as you drag, and React state does the rest.

name: BassoonTracker
capabilities: BassoonTracker recreates the Amiga tracker workbench in a canvas: beveled pixel panels, scrolling hex pattern rows, per-channel scopes and VU bars, plus a MOD/XM replayer built on WebAudio. Here the complete app is embedded through its HostBridge hook and loads a ProTracker M.K. module that the page writes in JS, with seven synthesized 8-bit samples and an original 4-channel tune. The tracker's own controls all work: you can edit notes, mute channels or open the sample editor.

name: BeepBox
capabilities: BeepBox's npm package ships the same Synth and Song model the beepbox.co editor runs: chip waves, arpeggiated chords, noise drums, and a whole song that fits in a URL hash. Here an original 8-bar loop is written in code as BeepBox JSON, played by its Synth, and drawn as BeepBox's colored track and pattern editors; tapping the grid edits the live Song and the beepbox.co link updates from song.toBase64String().

name: html5bytebeat
capabilities: Gregg Tavares' bytebeat engine compiles a JavaScript expression like t*(t>>5|t>>8) and runs it per sample inside an AudioWorklet, in bytebeat, floatbeat or postfix modes. The demo runs the library's own compiler and ByteBeatProcessor on the main thread too, so the scrolling t-plot (256 samples per column), oscilloscope and spectrum draw the formula before any sound plays.

name: NexusUI
capabilities: NexusUI gives you the stock parts of a browser instrument — dials, a sequencer matrix, XY pad, envelope, piano, oscilloscope and spectrogram — as plain JS widgets that emit change events. One Nexus.colors palette re-skins the whole set; here an 8×16 matrix drives a Web Audio synth while the XY pad steers the filter dials.

name: webaudio-tinysynth
capabilities: webaudio-tinysynth maps all 128 General MIDI programs and the drum kit onto WebAudio oscillators and generated buffers, so a full GM synth with reverb loads as one small file and takes raw MIDI messages through send(). The demo plays Bach's C-major Prelude, typed in as notes, across three GM channels, with a per-channel program picker filled from the library's own timbre names and a switch between its FM and chiptune timbre sets.

name: jsfxr
capabilities: jsfxr rolls game sounds (coin, laser, explosion, power-up, jump) from a small parameter struct and renders the samples in plain JS, so you ship a few numbers instead of audio files. Here an attract-mode pixel platformer fires each sound from its own bank slot, the waveform is drawn from the actual rendered samples, and the sliders edit the live sfxr params through jsfxr's own unit conversions.

name: audio/ui
